n1965a012fa57: Eucosma giganteana is a specialist herbivore on Silphium spp. and a major limiting factor to the commercialization of Silphium integrifolium, a perennial oilseed crop. Although it is known that (E)‐8‐dodecenyl acetate works as an attractant to E. giganteana, it is unknown whether it responds in a concentration‐dependent manner, and whether this cue works throughout the season. Also unknown is whether these moths behaviorally or physiologically respond to other important semiochemicals, such as those emitted by conspecifics or its host. This information is important for developing volatiles for use in behaviorally‐based management of E. giganteana. To address our questions, we performed field trapping with traps baited with (E)‐8‐dodecenyl acetate, characterized headspace emissions from E. giganteana, and used EAG and flight mill analysis to assess response to (E)‐8‐dodecenyl acetate and volatiles derived from S. integrifolium and conspecifics. Higher loadings of (E)‐8‐dodecenyl acetate in the field trapping studies conducted in 2024 resulted in increased captures of E. giganteana moths on sticky traps, which successfully monitored E. giganteana through their full flight period. EAG showed antennal depolarizations, which confirmed E. giganteana perceive (E)‐8‐dodecenyl acetate. In addition, female E. giganteana perceive volatiles emitted by S. integrifolium whereas males did not. Despite eliciting clear antennal responses and showing success in field monitoring, (E)‐8‐dodecenyl acetate did not influence flight behavior during the flight mill experiments under the tested conditions. Altogether this study shows (E)‐8‐dodecenyl acetate successfully monitored E. giganteana through the field season; more work is required to deploy it in behaviorally‐based management IPM tactics.
n6b7bab67aa51: The Jinsha River, as the upper section of the Yangtze River, plays a key role as an ecological barrier, yet its dry‐hot valleys face severe degradation due to harsh climate and human activities. Four native Ziziphus species (Z. mauritiana, Z. montana, Z. mairei, and Z. xiangchengensis) were selected to assess their potential for restoring “valley‐type savanna” vegetation through field investigations, species distribution modeling, germination experiments, and interviews. Field investigations showed that Z. mairei and Z. xiangchengensis exhibit limited distributions and small populations, requiring artificial propagation and protection. MaxEnt models performed well (AUC > 0.9). Ziziphus montana occurs in northwestern Yunnan and is primarily limited by temperature seasonality (bio4), elevation, and coldest quarter temperature (bio11). Under future climate scenarios, its suitable habitat is projected to contract by 11.3%–20.4%, with the remaining highly suitable area retreating toward the Jinsha River basin. Bio11 is the primary factor influencing the distribution of Z. mauritiana, and its suitable range is projected to expand by 44.1%–119.1%. Seed heteromorphism was documented for the first time in Z. xiangchengensis, Z. montana, and Z. mairei, classified into Type A (2 carpels) and B (3 carpels) based on carpel number, with Type A seeds dominating (66.0%–94.8%). These two seed types showed significant differences in temperature response and dormancy characteristics. Four Ziziphus species displayed strong physical dormancy, removing the endocarp and cracking the seed coat results in a 100% germination rate, providing a practical solution for large‐scale seedling propagation. Based on assessment, Z. montana is more suitable for ecological restoration in the Jinsha River Basin. The population age structure is of the expanding type and serves medicinal, edible, agricultural, ecological restoration, and handicraft purposes. We advocate for community‐based “interactive” ecological restoration, using economic incentives to drive ecological recovery. This study contributes to ecological restoration, germplasm conservation, and local economic development.
nc9f46cb2bd4c: The cabbage beetle Colaphellus bowringi, a key pest of cruciferous crops, exhibits a multiyear dormancy strategy characterized by pronounced interindividual variation in diapause duration: individuals entering summer or winter diapause—though initiated synchronously within each seasonal cohort—may remain in diapause for periods ranging from several months to as long as 5 years. To elucidate the molecular underpinnings of this extended dormancy and its sex‐specific regulatory patterns, we performed a duration‐resolved, sex‐stratified transcriptomic analysis. Adult males and females were sampled after 0.5, 1, and 2 years of diapause durations and subjected to high‐throughput RNA sequencing. De novo assembly yielded 66,379 unigenes, of which 16,132 (24.3%) were removed as non‐arthropod contamination, leaving 50,247 unigenes that were used for all downstream annotation and expression analyses. Comparative transcriptomic profiling revealed a conserved adaptive strategy during prolonged diapause: patterns consistent with coordinated suppression of energy‐intensive metabolic processes coupled with increased transcript abundance of genes in cellular protection pathways—including antioxidant defense, xenobiotic detoxification, and protein homeostasis mechanisms. Sex‐biased transcriptional responses were observed: females showed comparable or higher numbers of differentially expressed genes in matched duration comparisons, with sustained transcript abundance of genes associated with reproductive processes and somatic maintenance, whereas males displayed greater duration‐dependent transcriptional remodeling, particularly in signaling cascades and physiological homeostasis networks. KEGG pathway enrichment analysis identified sustained activation of glutathione metabolism, autophagy, and lysosomal degradation pathways throughout diapause; notably, extended diapause (2 years) was specifically associated with significant enrichment of immune response and lipid metabolism pathways. Duration‐dependent dynamics in gene expression underscore that diapause is not a static quiescent state but a highly regulated, multi‐stage process involving duration‐specific transcriptional reconfiguration. This study establishes the first duration‐resolved, sex‐resolved transcriptomic resource for C. bowringi and advances mechanistic understanding of long‐term insect diapause—thereby informing the development of targeted, environmentally sustainable pest management strategies.
n1714ae3928e8: The home ranges, core areas, and daily distances traveled of 10 collared roe deer in the agricultural landscape of east‐central Poland were analyzed. We demonstrated the dependence of the home range size and daily distance on natural and anthropogenic factors. We first demonstrated a relationship between home range size and the wind farm impacts on roe deer.ABSTRACTHome range and daily distance traveled are the basic parameters of animal habitat utilization and emerge from complex interactions between animals and their environment. In this study, the home ranges, core areas, and daily distances traveled of 10 collared roe deer in east‐central Poland were analyzed. The mean home range size for all animals was 136.1 ha (minimum convex polygon of 95% of points), and 69 ha (95% kernel density estimation); the mean core area was 10.9 ha (50% kernel density estimation). Core areas were larger in males than in females and larger in the winter period than in the growing period. Home range size decreased with increasing forest cover and increased with the number of wind turbines. Core area size was influenced only by the sex of the animal and forest cover. Neither the size of the home range nor the size of the core area depended on road density or settlement cover. The relationship between home range size and sex, natural factors, including forest cover, and season, is consistent with previous studies. Mean daily distance traveled for all animals was 3.14 km, and was lower in the growing period than in winter, and in females than in males. The daily distance traveled also decreased with increasing forest cover. Our study indicated a new anthropogenic factor shaping roe deer's spatial behavior in agricultural landscapes (wind farms). We concluded that roe deer have probably adapted behaviorally to wind farms as a new landscape feature. They probably treat wind farms like human settlements, generally avoid them, and use habitats at an appropriate distance from the turbines. We cannot, however, exclude the occasional fleeing behavior of roe deer near turbines. Further research should include a more detailed assessment of the behavior of roe deer and other terrestrial mammal species under the influence of wind farms.
n0edafbbe2040: IntroductionScientific understanding of the spatio-temporal evolution of Production-Ecological-Living Spaces (PELS) and their driving factors provides theoretical support and practical guidance for territorial spatial planning. This study aimed to investigate the spatio-temporal evolution of PELS and explore its driving factors in the Funiu Mountain area.MethodsDigital elevation models (DEMs), multi-source datasets of natural, social, and economic driving factors, and the geographical detector method were used to analyze the spatio-temporal evolution of PELS and identify its driving factors.ResultsFrom 2000 to 2020, the area of production space showed a shrinking trend, whereas the areas of ecological space and living space expanded. Among these, grassland ecological space and urban living space expanded significantly. Across different elevation zones, production space decreased in area. Ecological space increased slightly in low-altitude areas (<400 m), while changes in medium- and high-altitude areas were relatively stable. Living space increased across all elevation zones. Urban living space and industrial production space underwent the most frequent changes. In terms of spatial transformation, exchanges between ecological space and production space were dominant, followed by those between living space and production space, whereas transformations between ecological space and living space were infrequent. The evolution of PELS was primarily influenced by natural background conditions, while the driving effects of socio-economic factors became increasingly prominent. The q value of economic density increased 26.4-fold (from 0.0064 to 0.1688), while that of population density increased 7.5-fold, highlighting the increasingly important role of socio-economic factors in shaping the spatial pattern.DiscussionUnlike existing regional-scale investigations, this study identifies the elevation-gradient differentiation of the driving mechanisms underlying PELS evolution in mountainous areas. These findings enrich the theoretical understanding of PELS in mountain regions and provide targeted support for territorial spatial optimization and sustainable, coordinated regional development in the Funiu Mountain area.
nff4c6d1fb11a: Using a multi‐decadal dataset, we show the relative influence of predator recovery, annual weather, density dependence, and anthropogenic top‐down forces on a large herbivore. Intensifiying drought, driven by climate change, explains as much variation in population growth as all of the un‐modelled natural variation combined, highlighting the urgency of understanding large herbivore demography in a changing climate. Abstract Large herbivores play important roles in ecosystems across the globe, but limitations to study and inference have left gaps in predictive theories of their population dynamics, particularly following carnivore recoveries. Studies using spatial variation have explored the broad patterns of top‐down and bottom‐up forces in large herbivores. However, temporal changes in a population provide the most direct evidence for predicting future effects, and long‐term studies spanning variation in top‐down and bottom‐up forces remain rare. We used 36 years of data on elk (Cervus canadensis) in the western United States in an integrated population model to test the effects of top‐down (Puma concolor recovery) and bottom‐up (drought) forces on pregnancy rates and age‐based survival across a range of elk densities in the context of human harvest. We then quantified the proportion of variance in population growth attributable to those forces relative to the influences of harvest, age structure and unmodelled variation in demographic rates. Both top‐down and bottom‐up forces had measurable effects on elk population dynamics, with puma recovery reducing survival in the first 2 years of life and drought reducing pregnancy probability and survival at all ages. We also found negative density dependence in pregnancy, consistent with bottom‐up control and positive density dependence in survival of young, consistent with predator swamping. Harvest explained the greatest proportion of variation in population growth (26%). Of the non‐harvest parameters, drought severity had the largest effect, explaining as much variation (16%) as all of the unmodelled changes in demographic rates. Puma recovery explained 13% of the variation, and density dependence explained 8%. Without more long‐term studies spanning sufficient ecological variation, the predictive abilities of large herbivore ecology will remain limited. With ongoing anthropogenic changes to the forces acting on large herbivores around the world, improving predictions will be invaluable to conservation.
naeb8b8e1e57b: The contemporary ecological crisis calls for integration and synthesis of vast amounts of mostly scattered and often hard‐to‐extract ecological information that is dispersed across hundreds of thousands of scientific papers. Recent advancements in natural language processing (NLP) and the emergence of large language models (LLMs) offer a novel and promising approach to this persistent challenge. Here, we present a replicable and adaptable workflow that automates the extraction of a broad range of biological interactions among species from scientific literature using LLMs. We provide a demonstration of this workflow by performing a large‐scale data extraction directly from a corpus of 83,910 scientific articles using OpenAI GPT‐4o. Our approach successfully extracted a network of 144,402 interactions between 36,471 taxa. Performance analysis shows that the model exhibits a precision of 89.5% with a recall of 70.0%, demonstrating that a general‐purpose LLM can perform complex ecological information extraction at scale for analysis and synthesis. Results depend on quality filtering choices and inherit biases present in the underlying literature, emphasizing the need for validation and quality control. Standardized outputs can be browsed, queried, or joined with existing interaction repositories and taxonomic backbones, facilitating downstream reuse and interoperability. Our case study shows that LLMs are capable of carrying out complex extraction tasks on key ecological data on a very large scale, paving the way for a multitude of potential applications in ecology and beyond.
n6d933fb60722: Solanaceae represents one of the most economically significant families among flowering plants. Genomic research within the family has primarily concentrated on some crop genera, such as Solanum L., Nicotiana L., and Capsicum L., whereas early‐diverging clades remain comparatively understudied. This study presents the complete chloroplast (cp) genomes of two species belonging to the tribe Salpiglossideae (subfamily Cestroideae), Reyesia chilensis Clos and Salpiglossis sinuata Ruiz & Pav, and performs comprehensive comparative analyses across representative Solanaceae plastomes, focusing on genome structure, gene content, repeats, codon usage, nucleotide polymorphism (Pi), and phylogenetic relationships. The cp genomes of R. chilensis and S. sinuata have lengths of 156,969 and 156,262 bp, respectively, and both exhibit the characteristic quadripartite structure. Their genome organization and gene composition were highly conserved. The plastome of R. chilensis encoded 112 unique genes (111 in S. sinuata), including 79 protein‐coding genes, 29 transfer RNA‐coding genes (28 in S. sinuata), and four ribosomal RNA‐coding genes. Comparative analyses revealed only minor sequence divergence between the two plastomes, with highly similar codon usage bias and repeat sequence composition. Phylogenetic analyses supported R. chilensis and S. sinuata as a clade representing Salpiglossideae, sister to Benthamiella patagonica Speg. (Benthamielleae), together forming an early‐diverging branch within the Solanaceae. Nucleotide polymorphism analyses revealed a mean nucleotide diversity (Pi) of 0.013 within the shared genes, whereas intergenic spacers exhibited a higher sequence polymorphism (average Pi = 0.028). Several hypervariable segments were identified as promising markers for Solanaceae species delimitation and phylogenetic inference. This work contributes critical genomic datasets and further clarifies the phylogenetic comprehension across the family.
na8af695b3446: Hulun Lake, one of the largest freshwater lakes in China, is currently experiencing significant water quality deterioration. Therefore, water quality assessment is of paramount importance, as it not only provides critical insights into the current pollution status of lakes but also offers a scientific basis for effective lake management and ecological restoration. Using environmental DNA‐metabarcoding data from 13 sampling sites in Hulun Lake in June 2023, our study explored the spatial variation of α‐diversity, the community composition, and phytoplankton index of biotic integrity (P‐IBI). A total of 431 phytoplankton species were identified across 10 phyla, 191 families, and 335 genera, with Chlorophyta and Bacillariophyta predominating. Biodiversity was higher in the northern and southern regions, except for the site XHK, but lower in the central region. P‐IBI scores exhibited clear spatial variation, with relatively high scores in the central and northern regions, except for the site XHK, indicating comparatively favorable ecological conditions. In contrast, lower P‐IBI scores were observed in the southern region, except for DNHWZ and GZ, suggesting relatively greater ecological degradation. The P‐IBI scores were significantly negatively correlated with Water Quality Index (WQI) values, indicating that higher biotic integrity was generally associated with better physicochemical water quality. RDA and Spearman rank correlation analyses revealed that ammonia nitrogen (NH3–N) and total organic carbon (TOC) were positively correlated with P‐IBI, whereas temperature (T) and total nitrogen (TN) showed negative correlations with P‐IBI, indicating that spatial variation in P‐IBI was closely associated with nutrient status and organic carbon availability. Lake management should integrate both P‐IBI and WQI‐based assessment approaches, providing a scientifically robust basis for the identification of environmental pressures and the diagnosis of ecological health.
n70c37a27d342: Heliconius butterflies rely on spatial memory to maintain trapline foraging routes, repeatedly visiting pollen resources along memorized paths. Increased foraging performance resulting from learning the spatial distribution of resources is thought to have driven the evolution of this specialized behavior. Here, we experimentally test whether prior experience in a spatially complex environment influences relative foraging performance in the pollen‐feeding butterfly Heliconius erato, a species with well‐documented behavioral, ecological and neuroanatomical specializations for spatial learning. We reared freshly eclosed adults in either an open cage or a cage that was matched for resource distribution but structurally divided to increase the spatial complexity experienced by the butterflies. We then tested them individually in a controlled foraging assay under familiar and unfamiliar environments. Butterflies reared in the spatially complex environment efficiently reached the feeder regardless of familiarity with the environment, whereas butterflies reared in the open environment showed strong context dependence, performing well only in the open cage. These results indicate that prior experience of a spatially complex environment supports greater foraging efficiency in Heliconius butterflies, highlighting environmental structure as a likely determinant of the ecological value of spatial learning in this group, with potential consequences for foraging behavior in natural environments.
n58f095855827: The quality of reference genomes is of utmost importance as they and the therein annotated genes and proteins serve as basis for many downstream applications. Although the current Western honey bee (Apis mellifera) genome assembly (Amel_HAv3.1) represents a significant improvement over previous versions (Amel_4.0, Amel_4.5), it nevertheless lacks certain protein‐coding genes present in those earlier assemblies. One of these “lost and found” genes is locus 409868 of Amel_4.0 and Amel_4.5 which is missing due to an approximately 160 kb assembly gap on chromosome 10 in Amel_HAv3.1. Here we show that the A. mellifera genome indeed harbours locus 409868 encoding matrix metalloproteinase 1 (mmp1) and that it is expressed in at least four different mRNA isoforms in honey bee workers. Orthologues from other insect species have essential tissue and organ remodelling functions during development and gene knockdowns at specific developmental time points are lethal. As adult honey bee workers show in addition an elaborate age‐based division of labour with drastic major morphological and physiological changes requiring extensive tissue and organ remodelling, leaving out mmp1 because of a missing gene in the reference genome, may mean leaving out a potential key player in development.
n1601c1acec19: A critical goal of ecology is to quantify mutualistic network structure across all ecosystems and organisms, as these networks often represent essential ecosystem services and therefore network metrics are often used as conservation targets. Some major gaps still exist, one of which is Neotropical bees, a group expected to contribute exceptional insight to ecological network theory, owing to the extreme diversity of mutualistic interactions characteristic of the Neotropics, as well as the unique global distribution patterns of bees. Elevational gradients are a useful tool for quantifying change in network structure, with results having direct implications for predicting resilience in ecosystem service provisioning. In this study, we compared mutualistic network properties of 28 Neotropical bee–plant networks, along an elevational gradient from 200 to 1500 m elevation. Bee species richness peaked at mid‐elevation while network specialization and modularity decreased with increasing elevation. Connectance and nestedness showed a statistically significant increase by elevation. Combining indicator analysis and the number of bee species collected from only one elevational band, the majority of bee species, 101 of 157 (64%), showed association with specific altitudes, and each elevational band harbored a unique assemblage of bee species, with 95% of beta‐diversity explained by species replacement. The highest elevation band studied represents the top elevation of these short tropical mountains, emphasizing an urgent conservation need for these bee communities throughout the tropical realms as temperatures rise. Our finding of high specialization in lowland mutualistic networks of the tropics suggests that previously documented patterns of higher generalism toward lower latitudes may not have included bee–plant networks from Neotropical lowland and mainland ecosystems; resolving this debate will have important implications for conservation and restoration action.
n29b718f2417d: The mountain bongo (Tragelaphus eurycerus ssp. isaaci) represents a rare and critically endangered subspecies endemic to the Afromontane forests of Kenya. This study investigated the seasonal dietary composition of the mountain bongo at the Mount Kenya Wildlife Conservancy and the Mawingu Mountain Bongo Sanctuary. We conducted a two‐year observational study on the reintroduced wild population, employing random focal animal sampling at 30‐min intervals during active feeding periods from 06:00 to 11:00 and 16:00 to 19:00. Following each sampling session, we allocated 10 min to collect plant samples for subsequent identification. The data collected included the plant species consumed, the time spent on each species and the specific plant parts browsed. A total of 80 plant species, representing 43 families, were identified as components of the mountain bongo's diet, encompassing trees, shrubs, herbs, grasses, ferns, creepers, climbers and rhizomes. Seasonal variations exhibited minimal effects on herb or shrub consumption; however, conditions during the wet season were significantly correlated with a reduced likelihood of tree consumption. Seasonal dietary shifts, with reduced tree consumption during the wet season, underscore the importance of conserving a mosaic of vegetation types to ensure year‐round forage availability for mountain bongos.
nb985e2ff1a5a: Surplus killing (SK) by large carnivores may generate high‐intensity mortality events in colonial seabirds. Here, we document repeated predation events involving Magellanic penguins (Spheniscus magellanicus) and pumas (Puma concolor) in Islote Lobos National Park (ILNP, Río Negro, Argentina). During the 2024–2025 breeding season, only four adult penguins with cervical injuries and no signs of consumption were recorded, precluding their interpretation as SK. In contrast, during the 2025–2026 breeding season, multiple high‐intensity mortality events were recorded at La Pastosa and Isla de los Pájaros, two islets harboring reproductive penguin colonies in the ILNP. Across all documented 2025–2026 events, at least 961 penguins were found dead, including 887 adults and 74 chicks. Carcasses exhibited cervical bite injuries and little or no evidence of consumption, while fresh puma tracks, feces, and direct observations of an adult individual within the colonies strongly supported puma predation. During the four consecutive breeding seasons prior to these events, population monitoring did not record mortality episodes of comparable magnitude and suggested stable population dynamics within the ILNP colonies. The mortality recorded during the 2025–2026 breeding season represented a minimum direct mortality of 3.52% of the local breeding adult population. These records represent the northernmost confirmed case of SK involving Magellanic penguins and pumas, extending the documented geographic range of this interaction by more than 1000 km northwards. They also suggest that repeated SK events may represent an important source of additive mortality for local penguin colonies. Our findings highlight the ecological importance of episodic terrestrial–marine trophic interactions and the need for continued demographic monitoring in coastal breeding systems.
n238f24b6e623: Medicinal plants face growing threats from climate change, habitat fragmentation, selective harvesting, and other human-induced pressures that may diminish genetic diversity and weaken evolutionary resilience. Recent studies in population genomics and landscape genomics indicate that resilience is influenced not just by diversity across a species, but also by how adaptive variation is distributed among populations and its connection to environmental gradients. In medicinal plants, factors such as geographic isolation, precipitation, temperature, salinity, and demographic history have been linked to population differentiation and potential adaptive loci. Genomic methods can thus shift conservation from outlining neutral diversity to pinpointing populations and alleles that may be significant for upcoming climates. Simultaneously, transcriptomic, metabolomic, and epigenetic research shows that genetic adaptation is enhanced by phenotypic plasticity and environmental modulation of stress and specialized metabolism pathways. Nevertheless, direct evidence linking adaptive genomic variation to fitness in wild medicinal plant populations is still scarce, and numerous at-risk taxa are deficient in genomic resources. In this study, we integrate recent findings that connect genetic variability, regional adaptation, molecular stress responses, and conservation strategies for medicinal plants. We emphasize landscape genomics and genomic vulnerability as tangible connections between evolutionary ecology and conservation, stressing the importance of incorporating adaptive variation, epigenetic plasticity, demographic history, ecological interactions, and habitat preservation. Future research should emphasize non-model medicinal species, wider geographic sampling, temporal genomic tracking, and field validation of potential adaptive loci.
ne828877f222b: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Plant litter input can affect soil organic carbon (SOC) decomposition, that is the priming effect. Variation in experimental conditions, litter characteristics and soil properties among individual studies has led to inconsistent reports of priming effects. We aimed to synthesize global patterns and drivers of the litter‐induced priming effect. Using meta‐analysis, we synthesized 621 observations from 118 publications and performed multiple statistical approaches, including mixed‐effects meta‐regressions and variation partitioning analysis. We showed that plant litter input stimulated SOC decomposition by an average of 42% globally, indicating an overall positive priming effect. Compared with leaf and root litter, stem litter, which had lower nitrogen (N) content, induced a greater priming effect, particularly in N‐rich cropland soils. Microbial biomass C also increased by an average of 45% following litter addition, with a greater increase under stem litter than under other litter types, consistent with the microbial N‐mining hypothesis. Experimental conditions, including incubation duration and litter addition rate, were more important in explaining priming induced by leaf and stem litter, whereas litter characteristics and soil properties, such as C:N ratio and pH, were more important in explaining root litter‐induced priming, potentially reflecting the relatively high recalcitrance of root litter. Furthermore, the effects of soil properties on the priming effect depended on litter characteristics, with particularly strong interactions observed for root litter, highlighting that root litter‐induced priming is jointly regulated by litter quality and the soil properties. We emphasize the importance of the specificity of litter type in regulating the priming effect. Future studies should comprehensively investigate litter characteristics and their interactions with experimental conditions and soil properties using long‐term experiments to improve global predictions of SOC decomposition via the priming effect. ncad595e900dd: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Soil salinization and alkalization often suppress microbial functional activity, triggering negative feedback loops in microbial metabolism, degrading nutrients and agricultural productivity. However, the impacts of saline versus alkaline soils on microbial metabolism remain unclear. We compared reclaimed coastal saline (S 1) and Songnen alkaline (A 1) paddy soils with their corresponding non-saline controls (S 0 and A 0) using models of ecoenzymatic stoichiometry, aggregate fractionation, amplicon sequencing and high-throughput qPCR to quantify microbial carbon (C), nitrogen (N) and phosphorus (P) limitation and their abiotic and biotic drivers. Our findings revealed that saline and alkaline stresses consistently intensified microbial C limitation by 24.79% and 90.43%, respectively, relative to their corresponding CK soils. However, the two regional soil systems showed divergent nutrient limitation patterns associated with contrasting physicochemical and microbial conditions. Saline soils exhibited acute microbial N limitation (VTN/P limitation = −6.51), which was associated with lower N availability, including 53.29% lower DTN than in alkaline soils, macroaggregate-associated N depletion, and bacterial-associated network reorganization. Microbial functional profiles further indicated greater genetic potential for denitrification and lower genetic potential for dissimilatory nitrate reduction to ammonium, with A 1 soils having 25.12% lower nirK/S abundance and 49.68% higher napA abundance than S 1 soils. In contrast, alkaline soils exhibited stronger microbial P limitation (VTN/P limitation = 9.73), which was associated with reduced P bioavailability, including 56.68% lower AP than in saline soils, greater P sequestration in silt+clay fractions, and fungal-associated network reorganization. This pattern was accompanied by stronger suppression of genes associated with organic P mineralization and inorganic P solubilization, with phnK and gcd + pqqC abundances being 28.27% and 25.19% lower than in S 1 soils, respectively. These results show that divergent microbial nutrient limitations arise from coupled soil physicochemical constraints, microbial community reassembly, network reorganization and functional gene responses, rather than from ion-specific chemistry alone. These results highlight organic matter restoration as a common priority, but indicate divergent N/P fertilization strategies for saline and alkaline soils. These insights provide a fundamental framework for targeted remediation of saline and alkaline soils and facilitate sustainable agricultural practices by integrating both universal and salt-type-specific methodological approaches. Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. 摘要 土壤盐渍化和碱化通常会抑制微生物功能活性，引发微生物代谢的负反馈效应，进而导致土壤养分状况恶化和农业生产力下降。然而，盐胁迫与碱胁迫对土壤微生物代谢的影响及其差异仍不明确。 本研究以滨海盐土(S1)和松嫩平原碱土(A1)改良稻田及其对应的非盐碱对照土壤(S0和A0)为研究对象，综合运用生态酶化学计量学模型、土壤团聚体分级、扩增子测序和高通量荧光定量PCR等方法，定量评估土壤微生物碳(C)、氮(N)和磷(P)限制特征，并解析其非生物和生物驱动因素。 研究结果表明，与各自对照土壤相比，盐胁迫和碱胁迫均显著加剧了微生物碳限制，增幅分别为24.79%和90.43%。然而，由于土壤理化性质和微生物特征存在差异，两类土壤系统表现出截然不同的养分限制模式。滨海盐土表现出强烈的微生物氮限制(VTN/P limitation = −6.51)，这与较低的氮素有效性密切相关，具体表现为溶解性总氮(DTN)含量较碱土降低53.29%、大团聚体中氮素亏缺以及细菌相关网络重组。微生物功能特征进一步表明，盐土中反硝化过程的遗传潜力较高，而硝酸盐异化还原成铵(DNRA)的遗传潜力较低。其中，与S1土壤相比，A1土壤中nirK/S基因丰度降低25.12%，而napA基因丰度增加49.68%。相比之下，碱土表现出更强的微生物磷限制(VTN/P limitation = 9.73)，这与磷生物有效性降低密切相关，具体表现为有效磷(AP)含量较盐土降低56.68%、粉砂和黏粒组分中磷固定增强以及真菌相关网络重组。同时，碱土中参与有机磷矿化和无机磷溶解的功能基因受到更强抑制，其中phnK和gcd + pqqC基因丰度分别较S1土壤降低28.27%和25.19%。这些结果表明，盐土与碱土中不同的微生物养分限制模式并非仅由特定盐离子的化学性质决定，而是土壤理化条件约束、微生物群落重组、网络结构重构及功能基因响应共同作用的结果。 本研究强调，有机质恢复是盐土和碱土改良的共同优先措施，但两类土壤应采取差异化的氮、磷养分管理策略。研究结果为结合共性改良措施与盐分类型特异性调控途径，实现盐土和碱土的精准修复及农业可持续利用提供了重要的理论依据。
n509fc2960604: Biodiversity includes taxonomic, phylogenetic, and functional diversity but the changes in these facets at regional scales remain unclear and often context dependent. Using 2.5 million citizen science observations of 1957 vascular plant species across 53 years in SW‐Germany, we assessed changes in seven biodiversity metrics. Rather than a general decline, we found different facets exhibited different trends in both direction and magnitude of change. Phylogenetic and taxonomic diversity change were mostly negatively correlated, and change in functional diversity was independent from the others. We identified the role of climate and human activity influencing the change in taxonomic and functional diversity, while phylogenetic diversity was also affected by geodiversity. Crucially, we detected consistent erosion of biodiversity hotspots across all facets, while areas with low initial diversity tended to gain species. These findings highlight the need to consider multiple biodiversity facets and local context dependency to better understand biodiversity change at regional scales.
ne6e4d4228ab9: Si could regulate plant C and P stoichiometry with potential ecological implications. By mobilising P and improving NUE, Si may help mitigate nutrient constraints on biomass production and shape plant performance. Furthermore, reduced plant C:P ratios translate into P‐rich and high‐quality litter, which may in turn alter litter decomposition and soil nutrient cycling. Abstract Silicon (Si) is increasingly linked to shifts in plant carbon (C), nitrogen (N) and phosphorus (P) stoichiometry. However, reported responses vary widely across records. A quantitative synthesis is therefore needed to understand the overall direction and magnitude of these responses. We conducted a meta‐analysis of 168 records to quantify responses of plant C, N and P stoichiometry and nutrient use efficiency (NUE) to Si addition. Overall, Si addition reduced C concentration by 2.3% and C:P by 5% and increased P concentration by 8% and NUE by 14%. Plant N concentrations and C:N ratios showed no significant response. Reductions in C and C:P and increases in NUE were stronger in Poaceae, whereas the P increase was larger in non‐Poaceae. The Si‐C relationship was nonlinear and differed between families, and the P increase occurred only in substrate‐grown plants, not in hydroponics. This suggests no single mechanism accounted for the stoichiometric responses across plant families. Synthesis. Si could regulate plant C and P stoichiometry with potential ecological implications. By mobilising P and improving NUE, Si may help mitigate nutrient constraints on biomass production and shape plant performance. Furthermore, reduced plant C:P ratios translate into P‐rich and high‐quality litter, which may in turn alter litter decomposition and soil nutrient cycling.
na8305f07c7d1: Genetic biocontrol approaches offer promising tools for managing invasive species. However, their success depends on species identity, demographic history and the genomic architecture of sex determination, which remain poorly resolved for many non‐model taxa. We integrated high‐quality genome assembly, whole‐genome resequencing and population genomics to evaluate biocontrol feasibility in invasive suckermouth armoured catfish (Loricariidae) in Texas. Mitochondrial phylogenies and genome‐wide SNPs revealed cryptic diversity, with distinct lineages from at least two genera (Hypostomus and Pterygoplichthys) exhibiting strong drainage‐level genetic differentiation. Effective population size estimates were exceptionally low, consistent with founder effects and moderate inbreeding. Genome‐wide association analyses detected no large‐effect loci for sex in either genus, despite high statistical power in Hypostomus, suggesting that sex determination is polygenic and/or environmentally influenced. These results identify key biological constraints for sex‐ratio‐based biocontrol and underscore the importance of genomic assessments prior to management interventions. More broadly, our study highlights how integrating genomic resources, demographic inference and evolutionary context can guide invasive species control strategies.
n643f4450393d: In a mature Scots pine forest (Pfynwald, Switzerland), canopy vapor pressure deficit (VPD)a was reduced with a misting system (a) and combined with a throughfall‐exclusion roof that imposed soil drought (b). Under the roofs (c), trees at ambient VPD closed their stomata steeply as predawn water potential (ΨPD) fell, reaching closure around −1.2 MPa. Trees under reduced VPD responded more gradually and gas exchange continued down to about −1.5 MPa. Lowering atmospheric demand therefore delays stomatal closure and extends transpiration during soil drought. Summary Understanding how trees respond to interacting soil and atmospheric droughts is crucial for predicting forest resilience under climate change. However, no experiment has yet jointly manipulated vapor pressure deficit (VPD) and soil moisture in forests, limiting our ability to disentangle their effects. We investigated how c. 130‐yr‐old trees respond to coupled soil and atmospheric drought with a rainfall and VPD manipulation in an unmanaged forest. Using fine mist sprayers installed at canopy height, we reduced VPD by 24% in combination with throughfall exclusion (−50% precipitation) or irrigation (+100% precipitation) in mature Pinus sylvestris trees. We monitored tree water status, canopy conductance, and stomatal responses throughout the growing season. With irrigation, VPD reduction did not affect tree water relations. Under soil drought, trees exposed to reduced VPD used more water and reached lower predawn water potentials (ΨPD). This was accompanied by two parallel mechanisms: more frequently open stomata (at low‐VPD intensities); and a modification in the stomatal response to VPD. Moreover, reduced VPD resulted in shifted stomatal closure from a predawn water potential of −1.2 to −1.5 MPa. Exposure to low atmospheric demand affected trees' response to soil drought, providing observational evidences from joint air‐soil drought manipulation in natura.
n14aae493be54: Design of the VPDrought experiment in a Scots pine (Pinus sylvestris) forest at the Pfynwald research platform. Summary Atmospheric and soil drought are major, yet typically confounded, drivers of tree stress. Rising vapor pressure deficit (VPD) may impair forest function independently of soil moisture decline, yet stand‐scale experimental separation in mature forests has remained unresolved. We tested whether atmospheric demand can be manipulated independently of soil water supply and how such manipulation propagates through the soil–plant system. We established a factorial field manipulation in a c. 130‐yr‐old Pinus sylvestris forest that independently modifies canopy VPD and soil water input using fine‐mist VPD reduction, irrigation (+600 mm), and throughfall exclusion (−50% precipitation). Atmospheric and soil conditions were continuously monitored across depths over two growing seasons. The experiment specifically targeted periods of high atmospheric evaporative demand, reducing VPD by an average of 21% when ambient VPD exceeded its 90th percentile. Soil drying followed sustained high‐VPD phases, beginning in the topsoil and progressively later at depth. Despite identical water inputs, reduced VPD particularly altered deeper soil water trajectories, indicating plant‐mediated feedbacks. Atmospheric drought propagates through the soil–plant–atmosphere continuum rather than acting solely as an aboveground stressor. Explicit integration of atmospheric demand into experiments and ecosystem models is essential for predicting forest resilience under rising atmospheric drought. Zusammenfassung Atmosphärische Trockenheit und Bodentrockenheit sind wesentliche, jedoch meist sich gegenseitig überlagernde Ursachen für Stress bei Bäumen. Ein steigendes Dampfdruckdefizit (VPD) kann die Funktionsfähigkeit von Wäldern unabhängig von einer Abnahme der Bodenfeuchte beeinträchtigen. Bisher ist es noch nicht gelungen, diese Einflussgrößen auf Bestandesebene in Altbeständen experimentell zu trennen. Wir untersuchten, ob sich das Dampfdruckdefizit unabhängig von der Bodenwasserversorgung manipulieren lässt und wie sich eine solche Manipulation auf das Boden‐Pflanzen‐System auswirkt. In einem etwa 130 Jahre alten Waldkiefernbestand (Pinus sylvestris L.) etablierten wir ein faktorielles Freilandexperiment, in dem wir das VPD im Kronenraum und die Wasserzufuhr zum Boden unabhängig voneinander variierten. Hierzu wurden eine VPD‐Absenkung durch Feinvernebelung, Bewässerung (+600 mm) und der teilweise Ausschluss des Bestandesniederschlags (−50% Niederschlag) eingesetzt. Über zwei Vegetationsperioden hinweg wurden die atmosphärischen und Bodenbedingungen in verschiedenen Tiefen kontinuierlich erfasst. Das Experiment zielte insbesondere auf Zeiträume mit hohem Dampfdruckdefizit ab und reduzierte das VPD im Mittel um 21%, wenn das VPD der Umgebungsluft sein 90. Perzentil überschritt. Nach anhaltenden Phasen mit hohem VPD setzte die Bodenaustrocknung zunächst im Oberboden und mit zunehmender Tiefe zeitlich verzögert ein. Trotz identischer Wasserzufuhr veränderte das reduzierte VPD insbesondere die zeitliche Entwicklung der Wasserverfügbarkeit in tieferen Bodenschichten. Dies deutet auf pflanzenvermittelte Rückkopplungen hin. Atmosphärische Trockenheit wirkt sich entlang des Boden‐Pflanzen‐Atmosphäre‐Kontinuums aus und ist somit nicht ausschließlich ein oberirdischer Stressfaktor. Die explizite Berücksichtigung des atmosphärischen Verdunstungsbedarfs in Experimenten und Ökosystemmodellen ist entscheidend, um die Resilienz von Wäldern gegenüber zunehmender atmosphärischer Trockenheit vorherzusagen. Résumé La sécheresse atmosphérique et la sécheresse du sol sont des facteurs majeurs de stress chez les arbres, mais leurs effets sont généralement confondus. Cependant, l’augmentation du déficit de pression de vapeur (VPD) peut altérer le fonctionnement des forêts indépendamment d’une diminution de l’humidité du sol.…
n8f6329b4819a: The phylogenetically conserved trade‐off between the investment in root hairs and mycorrhization formation. Summary Plants take up nutrients from the soil while investing in absorptive root surface or mycorrhizal partners. Root hairs – a major structure for nutrient uptake and cheap to build – increase the absorptive root surface. As such, they are an important component of plant resource economics but largely neglected in root economic concepts so far. This is mainly due to data scarcity, which we set out to overcome by measuring root‐hair traits on 82 European grassland species in a glasshouse experiment. Using fluorescence and light microscopy, root‐hair length and incidence were measured along with mycorrhizal colonization. We found a phylogenetically conserved trade‐off between plant investment into root hairs and mycorrhiza, which captures functional differences between obligatory and non‐mycorrhizal plants as well as between grasses and legumes. This trade‐off defines a novel dimension in fine‐root trait variation. We conclude that plants invest in root hairs as part of a ‘do‐it‐yourself’ strategy in absorptive surface maximization for soil exploration. These findings demonstrate that root hairs play a fundamental role in fine‐root trait variation and need to be considered when studying belowground plant economic strategies. Zusammenfassung Um Nährstoffe aus dem Boden aufzunehmen, investieren Pflanzen in Wurzeloberfläche oder Mykorrhiza‐Partner. Wurzelhaare – wichtige Strukturen für die Nährstoffaufnahme, die günstig gebildet werden können – vergrößern die absorbierende Wurzeloberfläche. Damit sind sie ein wichtiger Bestandteil der Ressourcenökonomie von Pflanzen, wurden jedoch in Konzepten der Wurzelökonomie bislang weitgehend vernachlässigt. Dies ist hauptsächlich auf die geringe Datenverfügbarkeit zurückzuführen, die wir durch die Messung von Wurzelhaarmerkmalen an 82 europäischen Grünlandarten in einem Gewächshausexperiment ein Stück weit überwinden wollten. Mithilfe von Fluoreszenz‐ und Lichtmikroskopie wurden die Länge und das Vorkommen von Wurzelhaaren sowie die Mykorrhiza‐Kolonisierung gemessen. Wir fanden einen phylogenetisch konservierten Trade‐off zwischen den Investitionen der Pflanzen in Wurzelhaare und Mykorrhiza. Dieser stellte funktionelle Unterschiede zwischen obligat mykorrhizalen und nicht‐mykorrhizalen Pflanzen sowie zwischen Gräsern und Leguminosen dar und definierte eine neue Dimension der Merkmalsvariation von Feinwurzeln Wir kommen zu dem Schluss, dass Pflanzen im Rahmen einer „Do‐it‐yourself“‐Strategie zur Maximierung der absorbierenden Oberfläche für die Erschließung des Bodens in Wurzelhaare investieren können. Unsere Ergebnisse zeigen, dass Wurzelhaare eine grundlegende Rolle bei der Merkmalsvariation von Feinwurzeln spielen und bei der Untersuchung unterirdischer pflanzlicher Ressourcenstrategien berücksichtigt werden müssen.
n0ce6c4ee7fb0: Behavior is a critical but underexplored component of biodiversity, often overlooked in conservation science, ecological restoration, and biodiversity management. We argue that behavioral diversity needs to be formally recognized as a distinct facet of biodiversity, given its critical value as a reservoir of adaptive potential, and that current gaps in knowledge should be acknowledged as what we formally define to be a behavioral diversity knowledge shortfall. Present knowledge shortfalls need to be confronted by establishing standardized behavioral diversity indicators, harnessing recent technological developments and large databases, building capacity, promoting interdisciplinary collaboration, and setting research priorities. Recognizing and reducing the behavioral diversity knowledge shortfall will help better explain existing biodiversity patterns and improve the outcomes of conservation actions.
nb96c0a397cf1: Despite decades of international agreements aimed at biodiversity conservation, millions of migratory birds continue to be illegally killed each year along the African–Eurasian flyway, particularly in the Mediterranean, posing a persistent challenge to global conservation efforts. We compared legal frameworks in 10 countries to determine how implementation gaps have emerged between conservation legislation and enforcement. Using purposive sampling and comparative legal analysis, we examined how international conservation conventions and EU directives have been translated into national legislation and implemented in practice. Our findings revealed a fragmented conservation governance system in which enforcement consistently lags behind legal commitments, contributing to continued biodiversity loss, including the 78% decline in the European turtle dove (Streptopelia turtur) since 1980. Across diverse legal and institutional settings, cultural traditions, economic incentives associated with hunting tourism, and lobbying pressures have repeatedly weakened compliance and enforcement. Although legal penalties range from modest administrative fines to criminal sanctions, inconsistent enforcement limits their deterrent effect. By identifying common patterns across multiple jurisdictions, we identified the institutional factors that sustain implementation gaps and argue that narrowing these gaps will require stronger political commitment, greater enforcement capacity, and explicit recognition of wildlife crime as a serious conservation and environmental offense. Análisis jurídico comparativo de la conservación de aves migratorias a lo largo de la ruta afro‐euroasiática Resumen A pesar de décadas de acuerdos internacionales destinados a la conservación de la biodiversidad, cada año se siguen matando ilegalmente millones de aves migratorias a lo largo de la ruta migratoria afro‐euroasiática, especialmente en el Mediterráneo, lo que supone un desafío persistente para los esfuerzos de conservación a nivel mundial. Comparamos los marcos jurídicos de diez países para determinar cómo han surgido los vacíos de aplicación entre la legislación en materia de conservación y su cumplimiento. Usamos un muestreo intencional y un análisis jurídico comparativo para examinar cómo se han transpuesto a la legislación nacional y se han aplicado en la práctica los convenios internacionales de conservación y las directivas de la UE. Nuestros resultados revelaron un sistema de gobernanza de la conservación fragmentado, en el que la aplicación de la ley va sistemáticamente a la zaga de los compromisos legales, lo que contribuye a la pérdida continua de biodiversidad, incluida la disminución del 78% de la tórtola europea (Streptopelia turtur) desde 1980. En diversos contextos jurídicos e institucionales, las tradiciones culturales, los incentivos económicos asociados al turismo cinegético y las presiones de los grupos de interés han debilitado repetidamente el cumplimiento y la aplicación de la ley. Aunque las sanciones legales van desde modestas multas administrativas hasta sanciones penales, la aplicación inconsistente limita su efecto disuasorio. Cuando identificamos patrones comunes en múltiples jurisdicciones, logramos determinar los factores institucionales que perpetúan las deficiencias en la aplicación de la normativa y sostenemos que, para reducir dichas deficiencias, es necesario un compromiso político más firme, una mayor capacidad de aplicación de la ley y el reconocimiento explícito de los delitos contra la fauna silvestre como infracciones graves en materia de conservación y medio ambiente.
n95705162f84b: Threatened species that are societally extinct, which refers to the loss of a species’ presence in human societies, are less likely to receive conservation attention, potentially resulting in their biological extinction going unnoticed. However, little is known about the process and forms of such extinction. Thus, we aimed to quantitatively demonstrate the concept of societal extinction. We hypothesized that societal extinction leads to reduced conservation efforts for the affected species, which may, in turn, be associated with their biological extinction. We developed a framework for the trajectories between societal and biological extinction that involves four corner states and nine pathways of societal presence that can be characterized using quantitative metrics. A case study was conducted using Google Trends data for species listed on the 2020 Japanese Red List, together with information on private‐sector contributions to conservation. Notably, more than half of the species remained societally threatened, meaning they were close to societal extinction. In contrast, conservation efforts, such as tax donation schemes and nonmonetary corporate contributions, were primarily directed toward societally extant (particularly prevalent) species that were consistently searched over time. A small number of biologically extant species were nevertheless societally threatened, suggesting a potential divergence between the biological and societal status of species. Thus, species that are not only biologically but also societally threatened should be prioritized as targets for public conservation efforts, as they are less likely to receive sufficient support from the private sector. To inform future research efforts, we also summarized data on the societal presence of a selection of species from multiple perspectives beyond Google Trends. Un marco de trabajo para evaluar las trayectorias de la extinción biológica y social Resumen Las especies amenazadas que se encuentran en situación de extinción social, término que hace referencia a la pérdida de la presencia de una especie en las sociedades humanas, tienen menos probabilidades de ser objeto de medidas de conservación, lo que podría dar lugar a que su extinción biológica pase desapercibida. Sin embargo, se sabe muy poco sobre el proceso y las formas que adopta dicha extinción. Por ello, nuestro objetivo fue demostrar cuantitativamente el concepto de extinción social. Planteamos la hipótesis de que la extinción social conduce a una reducción de los esfuerzos de conservación para las especies afectadas, lo que, a su vez, podría estar asociado a su extinción biológica. Desarrollamos un marco para las trayectorias entre la extinción social y la biológica que incluye cuatro estados extremos y nueve vías de presencia social que pueden caracterizarse mediante métricas cuantitativas. Se llevó a cabo un estudio de caso utilizando datos de Google Trends sobre las especies incluidas en la Lista Roja de Japón de 2020, junto con información sobre las contribuciones del sector privado a la conservación. Cabe destacar que más de la mitad de las especies seguían amenazadas desde el punto de vista social, lo que significa que se encontraban cerca de la extinción social. Por el contrario, los esfuerzos de conservación, como los programas de donaciones fiscales y las contribuciones corporativas no monetarias, se dirigieron principalmente hacia especies socialmente existentes (especialmente prevalentes) que fueron buscadas de forma constante a lo largo del tiempo. No obstante, un pequeño número de especies biológicamente existentes se encontraban amenazadas desde el punto de vista social, lo que sugiere una posible divergencia entre el estado biológico y el social de las especies.…
n87aa8c30222d: Illegal and unsustainable wildlife trade remains a major conservation challenge and is increasingly shifting to online marketplaces where monitoring is difficult. To address this gap, we used real‐world images from online platforms, enforcement seizures, and market inspections to develop a deep‐learning object detection framework to identify products derived from three highly traded species: elephant, pangolin, and tiger. Our dataset of 39,941 images included both wildlife products and visually similar nonwildlife items, reflecting real enforcement complexity. We used cross‐entropy and asymmetric focal loss functions to train Faster Region‐based convolutional neural network (Faster R‐CNN) models and compared species‐specific and multispecies training strategies. The best‐performing model, trained with cross‐entropy on all species combined, achieved an overall accuracy of 84.2%, with high performance for pangolin (93.6%) and tiger (90.3%) and moderate performance for elephant (71.1%). Although asymmetric focal loss increased recall, it substantially reduced precision. We deployed the optimized model in a prototype smartphone application, potentially usable in real‐world settings for monitoring online images. With an independent test set, the application achieved 91.3% accuracy and an F‐score of 0.86. These results demonstrate the potential of object detection models to support scalable, real‐time monitoring of wildlife trade and enable the rapid triage of suspicious posts, regulatory compliance, and conservation decision‐making. Detección del comercio en productos derivados de especies amenazadas mediante aprendizaje automatizado y aplicaciones en teléfonos inteligentes Resumen El comercio ilegal e insostenible de fauna silvestre sigue siendo un importante reto para la conservación y se está desplazando cada vez más hacia los mercados en línea, donde resulta difícil llevar a cabo una vigilancia eficaz. Para enfrentar esta carencia, utilizamos imágenes reales procedentes de plataformas en línea, incautaciones realizadas por las fuerzas del orden e inspecciones de mercado para desarrollar un marco de detección de objetos basado en el aprendizaje profundo, con el fin de identificar productos derivados de tres especies muy comercializadas: el elefante, el pangolín y el tigre. Nuestro conjunto de datos, compuesto por 39, 941 imágenes, incluía tanto productos de fauna silvestre como artículos no silvestres visualmente similares, lo que refleja la complejidad real de la labor de las fuerzas del orden. Utilizamos funciones de entropía cruzada y de pérdida focal asimétrica para entrenar modelos de red neuronal convolucional basada en regiones más rápidas (faster R‐CNN) y comparamos estrategias de entrenamiento específicas para cada especie y multiespecíficas. El modelo con mejor rendimiento, entrenado con entropía cruzada sobre todas las especies combinadas, alcanzó una precisión global del 84.2%, con un alto rendimiento para el pangolín (93.6%) y el tigre (90.3%), y un rendimiento moderado para el elefante (71.1%). Si bien la pérdida focal asimétrica aumentó la recuperación, redujo sustancialmente la precisión. Implementamos el modelo optimizado en una aplicación prototipo para teléfonos inteligentes, que podría utilizarse en entornos reales para la supervisión de imágenes en línea. Con un conjunto de datos de prueba independiente, la aplicación alcanzó una precisión del 91.3% y un índice F de 0.86. Estos resultados demuestran el potencial de los modelos de detección de objetos para facilitar una vigilancia escalable y en tiempo real del comercio de fauna silvestre, así como para permitir la rápida clasificación de publicaciones sospechosas, el cumplimiento normativo y la toma de decisiones en materia de conservación.
n764ab28b453a: Understanding seed‐dispersal of Rafflesiaceae species is essential to conserve this extraordinary family of parasitic plants. We present evidence supporting diplochorous seed dispersal, involving primary endozoochorous dispersal by small mammals, followed by secondary exozoochorous dispersal by dung beetles. Methods employed included in situ live capture of small mammals in traps, placed over developing Sapria himalayana fruits, in situ observations of dung beetles handling the small dung pellets of primary dispersers and ex situ experiments with both dispersers. Dung pellet analyses (number, weight, expulsion time and ratio of undamaged to broken seeds) indicated that the most capable primary seed dispersers were the nocturnal rat Maxomys surifer (among four species studied) and, during daytime, the squirrel Dremomys rufigenis and, to a lesser extent, the treeshrew Tupaia belangeri. Dispersal distances were likely to encompass multiple host Tetrastigma spp. (lianas). Dung beetles served as secondary dispersers. They removed all faecal pellets of primary dispersers from the soil surface within 24 h, burying them up to 7 cm deep. The beetles also released seeds from the faecal matrix by microphagy, enabling the seeds to come into intimate contact with hosts' fine roots and root hairs, through which infection likely occurs. Forty‐one beetle species (including seven new species) were involved, with Ochicanthon thai and Onthophagus lindaae being the most abundant. Further research throughout the distribution of Rafflesiaceae species, particularly in the Philippines, regarded as a centre of Rafflesia diversity, is likely to add to primary and secondary disperser diversity.
n8021a35a6068: Biodiversity conservation and management in highly urbanized estuaries have garnered widespread global attention. However, the environmental response mechanisms of fish communities in these estuaries remain poorly understood, hindering their ecological health and sustainable development. Here, we utilized Hierarchical Modeling of Species Communities (HMSC), a burgeoning and powerful framework, jointly investigating how the species occurrences, species traits, and spatiotemporal structure of fish communities respond to environmental variables in the Pearl River Estuary (PRE). It exhibited seasonal variation in species composition, taxonomic diversity, functional diversity, and functional‐space occupancy of fish communities, and several CWM traits showed directional seasonal shifts. Furthermore, the HMSC framework showed that environmental filtering was the primary driver of the spatiotemporal dynamics in fish community. Salinity, pH, and phosphate were identified as key environmental drivers of species distributions and trait‐mediated responses. Functional traits showed contrasting responses along the phosphate gradient, whereas habitat‐level residual species associations revealed distinct positive and negative co‐occurrence patterns that reflect shared environmental filtering rather than stochastic assembly. The study elucidates the environmental response mechanisms of fish community dynamics by integrating taxonomic and functional diversity perspectives, offering new insights into the assembly of estuarine fish communities.
nd252ab48d316: The white‐footed mouse, Peromyscus leucopus, is a generalist species found throughout the eastern and central United States that serves as an important reservoir for many tick‐borne pathogens relevant to human health. Patterns of P. leucopus relative abundance within small mammal communities have been shown to correlate with the prevalence of Borrelia burgdorferi, the main causative agent of Lyme disease, in vector species. However, efforts to investigate patterns of P. leucopus population size and small mammal community structure often lack geographic variation. In this study, we characterized patterns of P. leucopus population size and small mammal community species richness across a broad geographic range in Pennsylvania. Population sizes and small mammal community richness values in northeastern Pennsylvania (mean N̂$$ \hat{N} $$ = 28.6; mean richness = 5.3) were greater than those in northwestern Pennsylvania (mean N̂$$ \hat{N} $$ = 19.7; mean richness = 2.8). Projected changes in climate and the expansion of human‐caused disturbance have the potential to greatly influence the prevalence of P. leucopus in small mammal communities, so regular characterizations of P. leucopus community dynamics will likely be helpful to inform projections and assessments of human exposure to tick‐borne pathogen risk.
n998163711c0e: As habitat fragmentation intensifies due to Anthropocene impacts, ecological variation across spatial scales may cause conservation strategies to misalign with species' actual needs. Understanding how cross‐scale spatial heterogeneity in ecological variables shapes species distributions is therefore critical to optimize conservation prioritization. The Critically Endangered Hainan gibbon is restricted to highly degraded forests, yet the interplay of ecological drivers shaping its current distribution, from macro‐environmental constraints to fine‐scale habitat selection, remains poorly quantified. This study integrates two‐year monitoring data from all seven known Hainan gibbon groups (GA‐GG, representing the global population) using a multi‐scale sampling design. We employed 395 population‐level and 135 group‐level plots to evaluate 23 ecological variables spanning macro‐ (e.g., climate) to micro‐scales (e.g., food plant diversity), identifying drivers of gibbon distribution. We found that population‐scale distribution is driven by climatic and topographic factors (e.g., precipitation, elevation), whereas group‐scale distribution responded to fine‐scale habitat features (e.g., food plant diversity, terrain ruggedness, crown area). GC distribution reflects optimal foraging (preference for food plant diversity), whereas GE adopts an energy‐conserving strategy (selecting complex terrain with high food plant abundance). Habitat suitability followed a J‐shaped threshold response at the population scale, and divergent responses at the group level (rapid in GE, stable in GC). These findings underscore the need for scale‐ and habitat‐specific conservation: expanding climatically and vegetatively suitable areas at the population level, restoring food availability in GE habitats, and maintaining stability in GC habitats. Our multi‐scale mechanistic framework provides actionable conservation insights, with applications for other range‐restricted species in fragmented landscapes.
n4b9cc692d57b: The health of desert plant life is closely linked to the stability of the local ecological equilibrium, where both human actions and shifts in climate serve as primary influences on environmental security. This research examined the temporal and spatial variations in vegetation NDVI and climatic elements within the Kubuqi Desert between 2000 and 2023. It utilized partial correlation analysis, multiple linear regression, and the geodetector method to uncover the underlying drivers of NDVI dynamics. Additionally, the study applied an ARIMA model to forecast the NDVI trajectory for the upcoming five-year period. The findings indicated that: (1) Plant life in the Kubuqi Desert has experienced substantial enhancement, with more than 80.61% of the region demonstrating a highly notable upward trajectory in NDVI; nonetheless, the general vegetation is projected to display slight anti-persistence going forward. (2) Annual precipitation, annual average high temperature, and annual average low temperature all showed an increasing trend. (3) Land transfer mainly occurred among barren land, cultivated land, and grassland, with the conversion from barren land to grassland accounting for 15.49%. (4) Precipitation and high temperature are key factors affecting NDVI distribution, with a 2–3month lag effect on NDVI. (5) Vegetation NDVI will show an increasing trend over the next five years. This study will provide certain data support for vegetation restoration strategies in the Kubuqi Desert.
n56e58e4f3547: Using biometric data collected over 33 years in a Mediterranean population of Great tits we reveal a dynamic phenotypic mosaic where long‐term trends decouple from immediate thermal effects. By integrating life‐stage sensitivities, we show how ontogenetic buffering and life‐history trade‐offs contribute to shape avian responses to a changing climate. Abstract Global warming is widely associated with changes in body size and shape, with these variations typically framed within the context of Bergmann, Allen and the Temperature‐Size rules. However, evaluating phenotypic change only against these rules can limit our understanding of how immediate plastic reactions to temperature interact with long‐term trends. Also, phenotypic responses may differ among life stages, due to their different thermal sensitivity and life‐history role. We examined body size and shape variations across life stages in a Mediterranean great tit (Parus major) population monitored over four decades, during which mean annual temperatures increased by approximately 1.7°C. Adults were the life stage most responsive to temperature and their mass declined by 0.84% for every 1°C of warming, while wing length shortened. Instead, tarsus length, a measure of structural size, increased with temperature in both nestlings and adults at a comparable magnitude, consistent with Allen's rule. Nestling mass near fledging showed no thermal response. Among reproductive traits, clutch size tended to decrease with temperature without reaching statistical significance and egg mass showed no thermal response, yet total clutch mass, an integrated measure of reproductive output, declined significantly with warmer laying temperatures. Long‐term temporal trends did not consistently mirror these thermal effects. Adult mass declined across the study period, matching the direction of its thermal response, whereas adult tarsus length shortened over time despite lengthening with temperature. Wing length and nestling mass both remained stable. Egg mass declined and clutch size increased across the study period, despite their lack of thermal response. These results demonstrate that while warming can proximately affect body size, long‐term temporal trends can be decoupled from immediate thermal effects, and that mass and structural size do not necessarily vary together. This creates an underappreciated mosaic of phenotypic responses across life stages and generations, with potential consequences for fecundity, morphology and fitness. Our findings highlight the importance of integrating ontogenetic perspectives into evolutionary ecogeographic theory and raise questions about which ‘rules’ will govern the trajectories of avian populations under climate change.
ne434b73e4693: Repeated drought reduced resistance under the most severe drought conditions, yet this mesic grassland recovered rapidly once drought ended. At the same time, AM fungal colonization of the dominant grass remained reduced, revealing a mismatch between above‐ground recovery and below‐ground legacies and showing that different ecosystem components can recover at different rates. Abstract Drought legacies can shape how grasslands respond to increasingly frequent climate extremes, yet their influence on future resistance and recovery remains unclear, particularly in mesic grasslands, where productivity is strongly linked to precipitation availability. Using a long‐term field experiment, we tested how zero, one or two prior experimentally imposed extreme droughts influenced grassland resistance to a subsequent 4‐year extreme drought (2018–2021) and recovery after drought in 2022. We quantified above‐ground net primary productivity and species composition, as well as plant functional traits and arbuscular mycorrhizal (AM) fungal colonization of the dominant grasses at the site, to evaluate above‐ and below‐ground legacy effects. Differences in productivity resistance among drought‐legacy treatments were small during the first three drought years and became evident only in the final, most severe drought year, when resistance was lowest in plots exposed to two prior droughts. However, above‐ground productivity recovered to similar levels across all treatments in 2022, demonstrating substantial short‐term recovery despite contrasting drought histories. The dominant grass, Andropogon gerardii, exhibited higher specific leaf area and greater leaf production during the recovery year, indicating increased investment in rapid resource capture and regrowth. Additionally, AM fungal colonization of A. gerardii declined with repeated drought exposure and remained lowest in plots exposed to two prior droughts even after above‐ground productivity recovered. In contrast to these traits and below‐ground changes, species composition, including richness, evenness, turnover and absolute cover, remained stable across all treatments and years. Synthesis: Repeated drought reduced resistance under the most severe drought conditions, yet this mesic grassland recovered rapidly once drought ended. At the same time, AM fungal colonization of the dominant grass remained reduced, revealing a mismatch between above‐ground recovery and below‐ground legacies and showing that different ecosystem components can recover at different rates.
nf6f706723700: Seasonal and spatial variations in Leaf Area Index (LAI, or plant area index, PAI) are challenging to delineate in tropical forests because the changes are often too subtle to be reliably detected. Some software (e.g. CAN‐EYE) requires manual tuning of each image, making large‐scale analysis impractical. We analysed 19,044 images from four tropical forest subtypes and found that using coding‐free AI software to process hemispherical images can significantly improve the consistency of canopy‐sky segmentation, thereby improving the detection of temporal and spatial variation of PAI. The results show that replacing the auto‐threshold segmentation with AI substantially reduced inter‐software disagreement, with the mean inter‐software range for PAI decreasing from 4.31 to 1.19, and delineating correct seasonal and spatial patterns. CAN‐EYE could identify the correct seasonal patterns but produced less accurate results than the CAN‐EYE‐AI integrated approach due to subjective bias. The high consistency achieved after AI integration enables reliable cross‐site and temporal comparisons. As users can combine the AI segmentation with other DHP software, our integrated, affordable and coding‐free method offers wide applicability and high consistency of PAI measurements, facilitating the advancement of tropical forest monitoring and research.
na9f02e4678eb: Mechanistic models, expressed as simulations that can be run and visualised, are a powerful way to understand biological and other systems. Building them, however, requires formulating mathematical or rule‐based descriptions and translating them into working code, skills that many ecologists and other disciplinary researchers do not have. Generative AI can now perform much of this translation, making mechanistic modelling accessible to researchers, educators and students previously excluded by its technical demands. But delegating this translation to AI also carries real risks: modelling assumptions can become hidden, plausible but incorrect code can pass unnoticed, and the skills and critical habits that model building once developed may never form. We examine the benefits and risks of using generative AI as a modelling companion at each stage of model development (conceptual specification, formalisation, implementation and exploration), drawing on recent experimental evidence on AI‐assisted learning and on a worked predator–prey example built with AI, with a rule‐based epidemic model as a parallel case. At each stage we identify where consequential decisions are silently delegated to the AI and set out practical mitigations that keep human judgement engaged without requiring the technical skills AI has made optional: specifying the conceptual model explicitly before engaging AI, having the AI translate its formalisation back into plain language, testing the implementation against outcomes known from domain knowledge and designing the interface to support interrogation. This new opportunity is substantial: researchers, educators and students who understand their systems but have never been able to build models of them are now able to explore these systems mechanistically, testing how components interact and how the system responds to conditions it has not yet experienced, questions that correlative approaches alone cannot answer. Used carelessly, AI risks eroding modelling skill for little lasting benefit, but used deliberately, in the ways set out here, it opens a new pathway to mechanistic understanding without removing the critical thinking the old technical barrier once enforced.
nf3e3ff646f46: Pie charts illustrate the composition of fossil grass silica short‐cell phytolith (GSSCP) assemblages at investigated fossil sites in the United States and Türkiye and representative 3D meshes of classified phytoliths.
