Ecosystem‐function responses varied substantially among processes and baselines. Gross primary production was significantly higher in degraded than in reference streams, illustrating that elevated functional rates do not necessarily indicate reference‐like ecological conditions. Restoration did not consistently reverse degradation‐associated functional differences: denitrification was significantly lower in restored than in degraded streams, whereas nitrate uptake remained significantly lower in restored than in reference streams. Other restored–reference differences were generally weak or uncertain. Functional responses did not differ systematically among broad restoration‐measure categories. Restoration age was associated with changes in gross primary production and denitrification relative to degraded conditions, but none of the functions showed detectable convergence towards or divergence from reference conditions through time. In studies measuring both biological structure and ecosystem functioning, biological responses to restoration were generally positive relative to degraded conditions, whereas functional responses were more variable. However, the available evidence was too uncertain to conclude that biological and functional responses systematically differed. Our synthesis shows that functional recovery cannot be inferred either from restoration‐associated change alone or from concurrent biological recovery. Assessing restoration success therefore requires direct measurements of ecosystem processes and ecologically meaningful reference conditions that reveal whether functional change represents movement towards a process‐specific restoration target.
n8f7d196b3e26: Alpine ecosystems are experiencing warming, leading to alpine greening—an upward migration and enhanced productivity of vegetation. Although soils represent the largest carbon (C) stocks in these ecosystems, impacts of greening on soil organic carbon (SOC) dynamics remain unknown, especially in the high alpine zone. We measured SOC stocks, quality and radiocarbon (14C) based turnover rates along elevation gradients from (sub)alpine forests to periglacial zones on three bedrock types, representing trajectories of changes in climate and vegetation and weathering regime. Data were linked to SOC stabilizing pedogenic oxides (PO) to assess the potential of soils to sequester C upon alpine greening. Results show pronounced decreases in SOC stocks (from 10 to 1 kg C m−2) and increases in 14C‐based turnover times (from decades to millennia) with increasing elevation. This pattern followed a non‐linear sigmoidal function with a threshold at the vegetation line where grassland transitions to the nival zone. High alpine soils showed low SOC:PO ratios, indicating low C saturation and a high capacity to stabilize SOC on reactive minerals. However, negligible 14C‐derived carbon inputs suggest that low vegetation productivity constrains SOC sequestration in these soils. In contrast, towards lower elevation with a warmer climate, grassland soils receive higher C inputs, but appear more C saturated, leading to greater SOC turnover but little SOC stock changes. Bedrock influenced SOC dynamics with approximately 50% smaller SOC stocks and faster turnover rates in dolomitic than in siliceous soils, due to slower weathering and lower SOC stabilization. Using elevation as a space‐for‐time substitution, we infer that SOC sequestration under alpine greening will be confined to areas around the vegetation line, with parent material influencing the magnitude of C uptake. Future projections of SOC dynamics should account for vegetation shifts and bedrock‐driven stabilization to constrain the role of alpine soils in land carbon‐climate feedbacks.
n067c47a22454: Mechanistic eco‐evolutionary models are powerful tools for understanding how life diversified over geological timescales, yet estimating their parameters remains a key challenge. The high computational requirements of these models make probabilistic inversion methods unfeasible. We introduce INDITEK‐2.0, a novel Bayesian inverse modelling framework built upon the cost‐efficient and spatially explicit INDITEK diversification engine. To validate this framework, we conducted a proof‐of‐concept study. We first generated synthetic global distributions of current biodiversity of marine invertebrates using INDITEK with known parameter values. To mimic field data, some realistic random Gaussian errors were added. We then used our Bayesian inverse modelling framework to recover these original (true) parameter values from the dataset of current biodiversity distributions after 500 million years of diversification. We also conducted a suite of sensitivity analyses by disabling specific mechanisms of the model. Our solution is a probability distribution on the parameter space, and we show that the method successfully recovered the target parameter values with a relatively low degree of uncertainty. INDITEK‐2.0's ability to probabilistically infer underlying evolutionary processes provides a new, spatially explicit modelling tool for reconstructing the evolutionary history of biodiversity across Earth's ecosystems and taxonomic groups.
na88679fe8bda: Understanding how habitat and life history traits contribute to population genetic structure is critical for evaluating conservation risks and identifying optimal management of wild populations. Species derived from adaptive radiations can provide a useful model for studying such patterns because the presence of some consistent traits allows for closer examination of attributes which differ. Here, we examine population structure in rockfishes (genera Sebastes and Sebastolobus), a group of speciose, recently diverged marine fishes that exhibit a continuum of genetic structure, from cryptic species to putative genetic panmixia. In this study, we analyse low‐coverage whole genome resequencing data from nine rockfish species and identify four major types of genetic differentiation: cryptic diversity, isolation‐by‐distance (IBD), no detectable structure (putative panmixia) and no detectable structure with a single genomic region putatively underlying local adaptation. Two species, Dark (Sebastes ciliatus) and Northern (S. polyspinis) rockfishes, each exhibited cryptic diversity consisting of two sympatric groups differentiated at every chromosome throughout the genome. Black rockfish in Southeast Alaska also had two genetic groups, despite an overall signal of IBD from the West Coast of North America through the Gulf of Alaska (GOA). Five species showed evidence of genetic panmixia throughout the sampled range, while Yelloweye Rockfish exhibited high gene flow across ~4000 km, from southern California to the GOA, but had strong differentiation between the Salish Sea and the outer coast. Of the species in which no structure was detected, only Blackspotted Rockfish had one outlier region exhibiting signatures of potential local adaptation. Our results highlight how multiple mechanisms likely promote genetic structure in rockfishes, hinting at tentative links to depth distributions and offshore habitats that might influence patterns of differentiation in rockfishes more broadly. Further, this study provides genetic data for some of the most abundant rockfishes in commercial fisheries in the Northeast Pacific, enhancing the scientific information available for informing fisheries management.
ncd706c50dd10: Whether microbial community assembly is primarily deterministic (selection‐driven) or stochastic (dispersal‐driven) remains a central debate in microbial ecology. We investigated community assembly of bacteria and protists and their driving ecological processes in mountain Lake Tovel using a 5‐year 16S and 18S rRNA metabarcoding dataset. The frequencies of assembly mechanisms and their processes depend on the considered temporal scale. We assessed the influence of temporal scale (years, seasons, temporal distances from 1 to 48 months across all years) and year‐pooling (a common strategy in the assessment of assembly patterns) on the inference of community assembly in the upper euphotic (0–3 m), lower euphotic (3–25 m) and deep hypolimnetic (30–35 m) layers. Focusing on single years, bacteria showed more often different assembly mechanisms (both deterministic and stochastic) across layers and years than protists. Year‐pooling hid the inter‐year differences and preserved the signal of the most frequent single‐year process. A lagged effect of water temperature on bacterial community assembly was found, while an immediate effect on protist assembly. Bacterial and protists' niche width was generally independent of year‐pooling and increased with depth. Our study showed that different temporal scales and depth layers should be considered to gain a comprehensive overview on community assembly.
n21afa68ce109: Transposable elements (TEs) have long been hypothesized as a driver of lineage diversification due to their mutagenic ability. However, the correlation between rates of TE activity and diversification has rarely been tested, since it is challenging to measure the rate of TE activity in the deep past. Here, we investigated TE activity during the last ~150 million years of termite evolution. First, we determined the timing of TE amplification events using the sequence divergence of TE copies and identified two waves of TE bursts that took place synchronously across termite lineages, coinciding with the two major phases of termite diversification. Furthermore, we built phylogenetic trees using the presence/absence of orthologous TE insertions in the flanking regions of Ultraconserved Elements (UCEs), in which the branch length provided a measure of the rate of TE insertion/deletion near UCEs along the termite phylogenetic tree. The rate of TE insertion/deletion near UCEs predicted up to 34.8% of the variation in the termite net diversification rate. Overall, these results supported TEs as an important contributor to species diversification. More broadly, this study provided a phylogenomic approach to quantify TE activity in the deep past.
n4f9e7641d61a: Proposed working model of humulene‐mediated suppression of tomato bacterial wilt. Summary Microbial volatile organic compounds (mVOCs) suppress growth and virulence traits of soil‐borne pathogens, yet their ecological roles in disease suppression remain unclear. Here, we show that the sesquiterpene humulene from Streptomyces acts as a multifunctional regulator that suppresses bacterial wilt through coordinated inhibition of Ralstonia solanacearum, plant metabolic reprogramming, and rhizosphere microbiome modulation. We combined in vitro pathogen assays, pot experiments, microbiota transplantation, rhizosphere 16S rRNA profiling, root‐exudate metabolomics, and plant and pathogen transcriptomics to investigate the direct and microbiome‐mediated effects of humulene. Humulene reduced disease severity and pathogen abundance via a microbiome‐dependent mechanism. Microbiota transplantation confirmed that the humulene‐conditioned microbiome retains transferable disease‐suppressiveness. Humulene also selectively enriched antagonistic Streptomyces, not by direct growth promotion, but by reprogramming tomato root exudation to produce lipid‐derived petroselinic acid, which promoted Streptomyces growth, humulene production, and pathogen suppression. Root transcriptomics further revealed activation of lipid metabolic pathways involving alternative fatty acid desaturation and oxylipin signaling. Together, humulene functions as an ecological signal that integrates pathogen suppression, host lipid metabolism, and microbiome assembly to establish a disease‐suppressive rhizosphere, enabling microbiome‐informed control of bacterial wilt.
ncede0ec83ff8: Pest management often requires the rotation of insecticides, sequentially exposing non‐target populations to different compounds. In a two‐phased experiment, we assessed whether exposure to the pesticide chlorpyrifos induces rapid evolution in the non‐target species Daphnia magna and quantified the response of control and pre‐exposed populations to a second exposure to the same pesticide, another pesticide with the same mode of action (malathion), or a pesticide with another mode of action (deltamethrin). Chlorpyrifos selection induced rapid shifts in genotype composition and reduced genotype richness and strongly influenced population development following the second exposure. Chlorpyrifos‐selected populations outperformed control populations when subsequently exposed to chlorpyrifos and malathion but underperformed when exposed to deltamethrin. Our results highlight an eco‐evolutionary feedback in which rapid adaptive responses to a pesticide worsen the response when exposed to a different type of pesticide in non‐target species, increasing vulnerability to common agricultural practices.
nd9843bf3b157: Wetland ecosystems are highly sensitive to environmental variability, but the relative importance of hydrological and climatic drivers of colonial waterbird breeding is poorly understood in landscapes that depend on the tropical monsoon. We investigated the influence of wetland inundation and climatic conditions on the occurrence of nesting, colony abundance and species richness of colonial nesting waterbirds across nine wetlands in Tamil Nadu, India, over three breeding seasons (2022–2023 to 2024–2025). Breeding responses were quantified through systematic field surveys and related to wetland water extent derived from Sentinel‐2 imagery and climatic variables obtained from the ERA5 reanalysis dataset. We measured the effects of water extent, temperature, precipitation and wind speed with generalised linear mixed models. A total of 16 colonial nesting waterbird species were recorded. Environmental conditions during the 30‐day period preceding surveys consistently provided the strongest explanation of breeding responses. Water extent emerged as the dominant predictor of nesting occurrence, colony abundance and species richness. The nesting probability increased significantly with water extent (β = 1.732, p < 0.001), whereas colony abundance (β = 0.612, p < 0.001) and species richness (β = 0.275, p < 0.001) increased with greater inundation. Maximum temperature negatively affected colony abundance and species richness, whereas precipitation had weaker negative effects and wind speed had no significant effect. Our findings indicate that the main driver of colonial waterbird breeding dynamics in monsoon‐dependent wetlands is wetland inundation, while climatic factors exert secondary effects on colony performance and diversity. Securing suitable hydrological conditions will be essential to the conservation of colonial waterbird populations in the face of increasing climatic variability.
n82da3c76751f: Understanding the minimal genetic changes underlying the earliest stages of speciation remains a central challenge in evolutionary biology. However, most model systems used to study early speciation involve pronounced ecological divergence, making it difficult to isolate the initial genetic changes associated with speciation. Here, we examined genetic differences between the cryptic cricket species Loxoblemmus campestris and L. sylvestris, which inhabit the same geographic region without pronounced ecological or morphological divergence. Despite their morphological similarity, the two species exhibited small but consistent molecular phylogenetic divergence in both mitochondrial and nuclear genomes. To investigate genetic divergence between these species, we conducted population genomic and comparative genomic analyses. We identified amino acid substitutions that were common within each species across orthologous genes and evaluated their evolutionary probabilities (EPs) based on sequence conservation across Orthoptera. Although low EP amino acid substitutions occurred in multiple genes, three genes—Raf, Slit, and Sur-8—contained multiple such substitutions, and all three also showed elevated F ST values. These genes are functionally connected within the Ras/MAPK signaling pathway. These findings suggest that genetic divergence between L. campestris and L. sylvestris may involve changes concentrated in a limited number of functionally connected genes despite relatively few amino acid substitutions and limited phenotypic differentiation. Cryptic Loxoblemmus species may therefore provide useful systems for investigating early genomic divergence associated with speciation in the absence of pronounced phenotypic divergence.
n439d97498fe3: Sexual selection, defined as individual differences in reproductive success, can contribute to the maintenance of genetic polymorphisms through pleiotropic trade-offs between life history components. However, the extent to which sexual selection maintains genetic polymorphisms in wild populations remains unclear. Here, we explored genomic signatures of balancing selection and selective sweep in the northern medaka, Oryzias sakaizumii in Japan by performing whole-genome resequencing of wild individuals. In addition, we reevaluated the population genetic structure and admixture of Oryzias latipes and O. sakaizumii across the Japanese archipelago and identified genomic regions largely affected by introgression between the two species using F d statistics to distinguish signatures of balancing selection from patterns potentially caused by introgression. Based on multiple population genetic statistics, we identified 18 candidate genomic regions showing signatures of selection. In particular, a 100-kb region at 6.85–6.95 Mb on chromosome 18 showed high genetic diversity that did not show outlier for the F d statistics, indicating the extent of introgression in this region did not largely differ from the genome-wide average. This pattern suggests that balancing selection maintains genetic polymorphisms of the locus in O. sakaizumii. The overlap with a QTL for female mating behavior and the known molecular function of a gene within this candidate region for balancing selection suggest that sexual selection through female mate choice may contribute to the maintenance of polymorphism at this locus.
nfc365238506f: Active sperm guidance towards the eggs is necessary for gametes to meet within the fertilisation window and is usually achieved through the action of female reproductive fluids (FRF hereafter) on sperm flagellar movement. However, it remains unknown whether FRF retains this function in species with unusual fertilisation strategies, that is, that deviate from gametes being released in the open water or sperm being transferred directly into the female reproductive tract. Here we tested the sperm attractant role of FRF in the bitterling, a small cyprinid fish that parasitises freshwater mussels. Bitterling deposit sperm and eggs inside the mussel gills and gamete interactions are facilitated by the water current generated by mussel respiration. Because flow‐driven physical processes could facilitate sperm‐egg encounters, we argue that selection on active sperm guidance by FRF may be relaxed. Alternatively, sperm attraction could be maintained by pleiotropic effects of genes involved in other reproductive functions of FRF. Using a recently developed sperm selection chamber and the European bitterling Rhodeus amarus, we find that more sperm accumulate in the FRF channel compared to the water control. Moreover, European bitterling sperm showed no preference for conspecific FRF over that of a distantly related Asian bitterling FRF. Our results suggest that bitterling FRF resembles that of species with conventional fertilisation modes, implying that it could mediate sperm selection and cryptic female choice. We discuss alternative evolutionary scenarios underlying the persistence of sperm attractant properties of bitterling FRF despite the shift to a physically mediated fertilisation environment.
n6051f813b4d6: The Trindade petrel (Pterodroma arminjoniana) is a procellariiform seabird found on Trindade Island in the South Atlantic Ocean. Recent evidence suggests that it also ranges and breeds across the Western Indian and South Pacific Oceans, where it hybridises with closely related species. The fitness effects of hybridisation, and the extent to which these might vary among populations, have yet to be studied in detail. Some populations contain seasonally distinct breeding sub‐populations, but the causes and consequences of this variation are unknown. While whole‐genome sequencing (WGS) is revolutionising our understanding of eco‐evolutionary processes such as hybridisation and local adaptation, there is a lack of high‐quality reference genomes in the Trindade petrel clade. Until recently, whole‐genome assemblies in Pterodroma petrels were limited to a small number of species and were largely based on short‐read sequencing. Oxford Nanopore Technology (ONT) is enabling long‐read sequencing of non‐model species, and this approach has recently been used to generate a high‐quality reference genome for Pterodroma. Here, we use ONT to produce a high‐quality long‐read reference genome for P. arminjoniana. We first generated a de novo assembly that we then scaffolded using the reference genome of a closely related species, the Cory's shearwater (Calonectris borealis). The resulting assembly, generated from a male bird, was 1.25 Gbp in size, had a scaffold N50 of 85 Mbp, and a BUSCO completeness score of 97.6%. Our annotation identified 18,099 protein‐coding genes, of which 92.1% corresponded to lineage‐consistent avian gene families, and no contamination was detected. We also compared the new reference with other Pterodroma genomes using a multispecies‐coalescent phylogenomic analysis. Our P. arminjoniana reference genome will be a valuable resource for ecological and evolutionary studies of this species and its close relatives, as well as for comparative genomic research on Procellariiformes more generally.
nb7f7510bd627: Wolves and beavers increasingly co‐occur across the Northern Hemisphere, yet direct observations of their interactions remain rare, and little is known about how beavers respond behaviourally to predation risk under natural conditions. On 29 December 2024, a wolf killed an adult beaver on a foraging trail in Białowieża Forest, Poland, among the first video‐documented wolf–beaver predation events in Europe. Over the 53‐day monitoring period prior to the predation event, wolves visited the trail on 4 days, while beavers were active on 33 of those days (62%), averaging 4.9 detections per day (7.9 on days with activity). This contrasts with experimental work showing that predator cues alone are often enough to sharply suppress beaver activity. The predation occurred during hydrological drought. The watercourse above and below the pond was nearly dry, likely leaving the colony with nowhere safer to go. We interpret this apparent risk tolerance as consistent with the risk allocation hypothesis, where prey with no low‐risk foraging options cannot sustain antipredator behaviour without compromising essential foraging. Following the predation, the pond remained abandoned for at least 18 months. This expands on a previous report of ponds becoming inactive following wolves predating on dispersing beavers, suggesting predation can also displace established colonies, with potentially cascading consequences for water retention, nutrient cycling and vegetation dynamics. In drought‐affected landscapes, wolf predation could plausibly act as a spatial filter, disproportionately removing these ecosystem engineers from suboptimal habitats. This is a hypothesis that warrants future testing. As droughts intensify under climate change, this could compound into a feedback loop. Fewer active beaver sites would mean less landscape‐scale water retention, deepening drought and further constraining the beaver habitat that remains, and undermining the ecosystem functions that make beaver recolonisation so ecologically valuable.
nb2ad7ac91227: Rapid and unplanned urbanization significantly disrupts natural ecosystems and often leads to biotic homogenization across all climatic regions, including the tropics. The conservation potential of urban green spaces, including university campuses, remains relatively understudied, particularly regarding the divergent responses of different trophic groups within these ecosystems. University campuses are different from other urban environments in that their structures are primarily designed to support education and scientific research while conserving natural habitats. Here, we investigated the possibilities of taxonomic and functional homogenization within the tropical suburban environment of a university campus in Nadia, West Bengal, India, by studying the presence and functional characteristics of two phylogenetically distant arthropod groups, butterflies (primary consumers and pollinators) and spiders (top predators). Butterflies are often used as bioindicators, whereas spiders, which function as apex predators in urban ecosystems, serve to monitor habitat alterations. We performed systematic point counts for butterflies and visual searches for spiders across ten sampling plots categorized into three distinct habitat types based on anthropogenic disturbance (highly urbanized roadside, highly managed, and unmanaged natural zones). Taxonomic diversity was assessed using standard alpha diversity indices. Community composition and beta diversity were analyzed using Bray-Curtis dissimilarity, non-metric multidimensional scaling (NMDS), and permutational multivariate analysis of variance (PERMANOVA). To evaluate functional diversity (FRic, FEve, and FDiv), species were categorized according to key functional traits. We found high species richness at the suburban site, which remained consistent across all habitats. Our analysis showed a lack of significant community divergence, and functional diversity remained stable across different habitat categories in both groups (ANOVA: p > 0.05). Our results also indicated high functional redundancy for each land use. PERMANOVA test indicated that habitat type reflects a non-significant amount of variation in community composition for both butterflies (p = 0.413) and spiders (p = 0.886). These results demonstrate that different areas within a single university campus may not act as environmental filters for different species; instead, they support species assemblages based upon the available microhabitats. Overall, these findings highlight the importance of university campuses as functional refuges within urban biodiversity networks, emphasizing the need to maintain local botanical heterogeneity to conserve biodiversity.
n7cbb35f1e4de: Fire is an important disturbance in many terrestrial ecosystems across the globe. A byproduct of fire is partially combusted organic matter, or pyrogenic carbon (PyC), which can be difficult for most microbes to decompose. Pyrophilic fungi are fungi that can break down and use PyC, survive through extreme heat, and/or have adaptations to rapidly colonize under postfire conditions. However, only a few fungal taxa have been characterized for their pyrophilic traits. Understanding the growth strategies and pyrophilic traits of fungi found in post-fire environments can help us understand mechanisms of ecosystem recovery from fire and their contributions to carbon cycling. Here, we characterized the pyrophilic traits of seven fungal isolates (Trichoderma and Mucor species) by testing their ability to grow on different carbon substrates (media containing PyC, sucrose, or water agar). Isolates were also incubated across a range of temperatures to determine if carbon source impacts thermotolerance and if the ability to catabolize PyC co-occurs with higher thermotolerance. We found that PyC-associated fungi exhibited a wide range of growth strategies, and many were able to grow on PyC. However, we found weak evidence for thermotolerance and growth on PyC as coordinated pyrophilic traits. Finally, we also found high intraspecific variation in growth strategies and weak tradeoffs along the fungal economics spectrum growth traits. These results were additionally supported by FT-IR analysis of substrates and fungal tissues, which showed different tissue chemistry based on substrate. Our results highlight the importance of intraspecific variation in carbon use ability and growth strategy as a key area of future research for pyrophilic fungi.
n57ad5d265074: Wetlands are among the most diverse and dynamic ecosystems on Earth. Meanwhile, they have experienced habitat loss and degradation worldwide, leading to biodiversity declines. As a primary driver of wetland loss and degradation, fragmentation can pose profound impacts on natural environmental regimes of floodplain wetlands. Here, we investigated the composition of macroinvertebrate assemblages in the Heihe Floodplain, Northwest China comparing wetlands with connection to rivers (i.e., riverine wetlands) and those isolated from rivers (i.e., lacustrine wetlands), with the wetland type used as a proxy for hydrological connectivity. We observed evident differences in species composition and community structure of macroinvertebrates between riverine and lacustrine wetlands. Three indicator species (Palaemon sp., Radix sp., Gyraulus sp.) were identified for lacustrine wetlands, whereas none were detected for riverine wetlands. Compared to lacustrine wetlands, riverine wetlands had significantly lower taxonomic and functional richness, but they had significantly higher mean local contributions to taxonomic and functional beta diversity, as well as more heterogeneous communities at regional scale. Our study highlights the need for a balanced wetland conservation strategy that protects lacustrine wetlands with high local diversity while also maintaining or restoring appropriate hydrological connectivity to promote regional biodiversity recovery and enhance ecosystem service functions. It also underscores the importance of incorporating functional traits and beta diversity into environmental monitoring and conservation planning to safeguard wetland biodiversity and associated ecosystem functions and services.
n2cce92864e2c: Rapid urbanization and land-use change are reshaping ecological spaces in urban agglomerations, underscoring the need to identify conservation and restoration priorities under alternative development pathways. Taking the Yangtze River Delta as a case study, this study integrates landscape ecological risk assessment, morphological spatial pattern analysis, and circuit theory to evaluate ecological security network responses under business-as-usual, urban development, and ecological protection scenarios for 2035. To better capture the spatial heterogeneity of ecological resistance, landscape ecological risk was incorporated into the composite resistance surface together with land use, elevation, and slope, allowing resistance values to reflect differences among areas of the same land-use type under different landscape configurations and disturbance conditions. Multi-period validation yielded overall accuracies of 0.87 and 0.90 and Kappa coefficients of 0.81 and 0.85 for the 2018 and 2020 land-use simulations, respectively. Built-up land expanded most strongly under the urban development scenario, increasing by 6, 866.91 km2, whereas the increase was limited to only 54.37 km2 under the ecological protection scenario. Ecological risk exhibited a persistent spatial gradient of higher risk in the northeast and lower risk in the southwest, with high-risk areas concentrated primarily in highly urbanized regions. Ecological pinch points and barrier points were mainly concentrated along urban fringes and intercity connection zones. Comparison of the three development scenarios showed that the ecological protection scenario was more effective in constraining uncontrolled urban expansion and maintaining ecological connectivity. However, barrier points inherited from historically developed areas persisted under the ecological protection scenario, and their number did not decline markedly. This trade-off indicates that ecological protection alone cannot fully resolve regional connectivity constraints. Improving regional ecological connectivity therefore requires targeted restoration of persistent barrier points together with coordinated protection of ecological source areas and corridors.
ncca195ce37ce: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Biological invasions and heavy metal pollution are two pervasive environmental challenges threatening global ecosystems. While the elemental defence hypothesis posits that certain plants accumulate heavy metals to deter herbivores, it remains unclear whether invasive hyperaccumulators actively forage for these toxic elements and whether such below‐ground behaviour is dynamically induced by above‐ground biotic stress. Here, we investigated the foraging behaviour of the invasive hyperaccumulator Phytolacca americana in a rhizobox experiment simulating a dual‐stress environment of heterogeneous cadmium (Cd) distribution and Spodoptera litura herbivory. We considered root morphological responses and employed integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses to elucidate the underlying mechanisms. We found that P. americana preferentially allocated root biomass to Cd‐enriched soil patches when exposed to cadmium. Notably, above‐ground insect herbivory significantly amplified this below‐ground Cd foraging response. The interaction between Cd stress and herbivory markedly altered root morphology. Cd accumulated primarily in fine roots, where plants optimized their specific root length and tissue density to efficiently exploit Cd‐rich zones. Integrated molecular analyses revealed that Cd treatment significantly suppressed cytokinin levels in the roots. This hormonal shift likely promotes lateral root formation and accelerates heavy metal sequestration. Our results demonstrate that above‐ground biotic interactions can actively drive below‐ground heavy metal foraging strategies in invasive plants, manifesting as a complex morphological plasticity mediated by cytokinin signalling. More broadly, our study highlights how synergistic responses to multiple environmental stressors can enhance the adaptive capacity and ecological success of invasive species in contaminated habitats. Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. 摘要 生物入侵与重金属污染是威胁全球生态系统的两类普遍环境问题。元素防御假说认为，某些植物可通过积累重金属抵御植食性动物，但入侵性超富集植物是否会主动觅取这些有毒元素，以及这种地下行为是否受到地上生物胁迫的诱导，目前尚不清楚。 本研究通过根箱实验模拟镉(Cd)异质分布与斜纹夜蛾(Spodoptera litura)取食的双重胁迫环境，探究了入侵性超富集植物美洲商陆(Phytolacca americana)的觅食行为，解析其根系形态响应，并结合转录组学与代谢组学分析揭示其内在机制。 结果表明，在镉处理条件下，美洲商陆优先将根系生物量分配至镉富集土壤斑块，而地上昆虫取食会进一步增强这一地下镉觅食响应；镉胁迫与植食作用的交互显著改变了根系形态。镉主要积累于细根，植株通过优化比根长与组织密度高效利用富镉区域。转录‐代谢联合分析结果显示，镉处理显著降低了根系细胞分裂素水平，这一激素变化可能促进侧根形成并提高重金属觅食效应。 上述结果表明，地上生物互作可主动驱动入侵植物的地下重金属觅食策略，该策略表现为由细胞分裂素信号介导的复杂形态可塑性。本研究揭示了对多重环境胁迫的协同响应如何提升入侵物种在污染生境中的适应性与生态优势。
n3aaa24504891: Microclimate, the climate directly experienced by organisms, is crucial for understanding ecological responses to climate change, yet its long‐term dynamics and the drivers of decadal microclimate changes remain underexplored in ecology and global change biology. Microclimate changes do not necessarily track macroclimate trends. Changes in meteorological conditions (e.g., cloud cover, wind patterns) and vegetation dynamics (e.g., canopy opening, desertification in drylands, shrub encroachment in the tundra) associated with climate change can lead to locally divergent microclimate trends, thereby altering spatial variability. Understanding and quantifying how macroclimate change translates to fine‐scale microclimate change experienced by organisms, populations and communities is therefore essential for predicting ecological responses to global environmental change. This review examines how macroclimate change drives microclimate changes as experienced by life on Earth—and how these micro‐scale changes may, in turn, feed back into the regional and global climate system. Our primary focus is on near‐surface air and soil temperature—due to their relevance to most terrestrial organisms and ecosystem processes. The review is structured around three pathways of microclimate changes: (I) direct effects of changes in meteorological conditions, (II) indirect effects via vegetation changes, and (III) feedbacks between microclimate and climate change. Using three mechanistic model simulations in real‐world landscapes, we illustrate and quantify the key mechanisms that lead to divergent warming trends. We show that microclimate change emerges from interacting atmospheric, land‐surface, and biophysical processes, which can differ substantially across space and time. Predicting future microclimates therefore requires accounting for these processes and their temporal dynamics. By providing an accessible synthesis of these processes, this review aims to strengthen links between ecology and atmospheric science and improve our understanding of how climate change translates into microclimatic conditions relevant to life on Earth.
n4349a53349b5: Each year, billions of animals undertake migratory journeys, resulting in large transfers of energy across the globe. Population declines in many migratory species have affected these, reducing ecosystem resilience. We quantify the value lost and show how conserving migratory species can contribute to climate change adaptation and mitigation, and deliver socio‐economic benefits.
nca4a1d57cd4a: Using amino acid isotope fingerprinting, Sagi et al. show how Arctic wolf spiders shift between plant‐ and microbe‐based energy sources with changes in body size and plant productivity. This reveals how environmental conditions and consumer traits jointly shape carbon flow and link green and brown food webs in rapidly changing ecosystems. Abstract Animals influence biogeochemical processes by consuming other organisms, transferring energy from basal resources up the food chain. Energy is routed through plant, fungal and bacterial channels, and the relative importance of these pathways can shift across space and time. Variation in these pathways may be particularly pronounced in highly seasonal environments where resource availability fluctuates throughout the year. Spatiotemporal variation in the transfer of plant‐ versus microbial‐derived energy to higher trophic levels is poorly understood but can affect bottom‐up and top‐down processes. For example, seasonal shifts in herbivore versus microbivore availability (bottom‐up) may alter prey choice by generalist‐feeding predators and lead to changes in top‐down predator control on primary production and decomposition. We tested how spatiotemporal variation in primary production influences the use of different energy channels by a widely distributed generalist invertebrate predator in the Arctic tundra. We sampled wolf spiders across four sites spanning a productivity gradient in the Alaskan Arctic during peak summer and on a weekly basis at one focal site throughout the growing season. Using essential amino acid (EAA) carbon isotope (δ13C) fingerprinting, we traced the flow of plant‐, bacterial‐ and fungal‐derived EAAs to spiders and quantified the use of plant‐ versus microbe‐based energy channels between sites and across summer. Wolf spiders were associated with more plant‐ and less fungal‐derived carbon assimilation when larger or collected from sites with higher normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI). Across the growing season, spiders shifted from primarily assimilating fungal‐based resources in early summer to plant‐derived resources in late summer, aligning with seasonal increases in NDVI. These patterns demonstrate spatiotemporal variation in carbon flow through different energy channels and suggest subsequent top‐down predator effects may also vary with basal resource availability. Our findings also suggest wolf spider body size may predict whether predation indirectly influences primary production or decomposition. As climate change alters seasonality, resource dynamics and invertebrate body sizes, these insights provide a basis for predicting spatiotemporal variation in predator impacts on ecosystem processes. Finally, our work demonstrates the utility of compound‐specific stable isotope analysis for integrating ecological and biogeochemical theory through the conceptual lens of zoogeochemistry.
n681d8d777b6b: Camera trapping has become an indispensable tool in wildlife ecology, generating vast datasets that require efficient and robust analytical workflows. The R package camtrapR was originally developed for preparing camera trap data for analysis in external packages and has since become a standard tool for this purpose. The analyses themselves, however, still had to be conducted elsewhere. Here, we present a major update that transforms camtrapR into an end‐to‐end analytical platform that unifies data import, exploration, covariate preparation, activity pattern estimation, occupancy modelling and spatial prediction. All new functionality is available as R functions and through surveyDashboard(), a new code‐free graphical user interface that guides users through the entire analytical pipeline. Data import supports widely used formats, including exports from the Wildlife Insights platform and datasets conforming to the Camtrap DP data standard. Exploratory tools generate species accumulation curves, maps of species detections and activity patterns for up to two species. Covariates can be extracted at camera trap sites from user‐supplied rasters or online sources, providing inputs for model fitting and, as raster layers, for spatial predictions. Users can fit single‐species and community occupancy models, some of the most widely adopted analytical frameworks in wildlife ecology, and map predicted occupancy across space. Community occupancy models are fitted in a Bayesian framework using JAGS or NIMBLE. These hierarchical models estimate species‐ and community‐level responses to environmental predictors and improve inference for rare species. The workflow includes convergence diagnostics and posterior predictive checks for model assessment and produces spatial predictions of species occupancy and species richness. The workflow can be implemented both in code and within the dashboard. By combining a code‐free interface with advanced modelling capabilities, camtrapR now makes robust camera trap data analysis accessible to a wider audience of ecologists, wildlife managers and students. This paper accompanies camtrapR version 3 and serves as the reference for its expanded functionality.
n5bf3de55fe6f: Variation in warning colouration is common, despite strong positive frequency‐dependent selection favouring the most common morph and may arise from spatially or temporally variable selection or associations with other traits. We investigated the maintenance of warning colour variation in the wood tiger moth, Arctia plantaginis, which shows sexual dimorphism in colouration: two distinct male morphs controlled by a single locus, and continuous variation in female hindwing colour and larval warning signal size. Using whole‐genome sequencing of 657 individuals from a laboratory stock derived from a wild polymorphic population, we examined the genetic basis of multiple life‐history traits, chemical defence, pheromones and male activity. We specifically tested for associations with male colour and aimed to identify the genetic basis of female and larval colour variation. We detected separate major‐effect loci for female colour and larval signal size, which were different from the male colour locus. Hindwing melanism was the only trait associated with male colour, mapping to a nearby major‐effect locus and showing a link to reduced activity at higher temperatures. Female colour was phenotypically correlated with pheromone amount. However, apart from melanism, none of the traits measured showed an association with any of the loci controlling warning colours and we found no evidence that male colour is part of a ‘supergene’ or complex co‐adapted phenotype. Instead, our results indicate largely independent genetic architectures for warning colours, suggesting that variable selection rather than genetic associations may contribute to the maintenance of colour polymorphisms in this species.
ncecc71d2daa2: Model for PDK1‐AGC1.5/7 kinase cascade function in controlling pollen germination. Summary In flowering plants, the timing of pollen germination is crucial for successful fertilization and an important trait for seed and fruit crops. Environmental factors tightly regulate pollen germination, with germination‐suppressing conditions on the pollen‐producing anther and germination‐promoting conditions on the receiving stigma. Using genetic, biochemical, and cell biological methods, we show that this environmental sensitivity of pollen germination in Arabidopsis thaliana is regulated by a 3‐PHOSPHOINOSITIDE‐DEPENDENT KINASE 1 (PDK1)‐AGC1.5/AGC1.7 kinase cascade. We show that PDK1 hyperphosphorylates downstream AGC1.5/7 kinases to enhance their activity. Pollen‐specific phosphoproteomics identified multiple proteins involved in pollen growth whose phosphorylation is controlled by AGC1.5/7. Two germination‐promoting RHO OF PLANTS GUANINE NUCLEOTIDE EXCHANGE FACTORS (ROPGEFs) are phosphorylated by AGC1.5/7 at a novel site, reducing ROPGEF plasma membrane polarization. Loss of PDK1‐AGC kinase signaling resulted in precocious pollen germination on the anther, which was rescued by high AGC1.5 kinase activity. Conversely, AGC1.5/7 overexpression or a phosphomimic ROPGEF version inhibited precocious pollen germination. Distinct subcellular localization of PDK1 and AGC1 kinases upon pollen germination is likely to alleviate their inhibitory effect. Our data indicate that the correct timing of pollen germination requires the fine‐tuned activity of a PDK1‐AGC1 kinase cascade inhibiting ROPGEFs on the anther, preventing precocious pollen germination.
n9db5e84e811f: A working model of the core regulator CsBBX19 which fine‐tunes tea quality and cold tolerance in tea plants. Summary Early spring cold spells threaten tea plant (Camellia sinensis) yield and disrupt the catechins‐to‐theanine ratio that determines the desirable balance of umami and astringency taste of tea. However, the molecular mechanism coordinating cold tolerance with this key quality trait remains unclear. Here, we identified a light‐responsive B‐BOX DOMAIN PROTEIN CsBBX19 as a core regulator simultaneously shaping tea quality and cold tolerance. Results demonstrated that silencing CsBBX19 relieves the transcriptional repression of theanine‐biosynthetic genes (CsTSI and CsAlaDC) to elevate theanine levels, yet weakens the activation of catechins‐biosynthetic genes (CsANS1, CsANR1, CsLAR1, and CsSCPL1/2/5) to reduce catechins content. The CsBBX19‐modulated theanine accumulation also enhanced the cold tolerance of tea plants by suppressing cell‐wall‐loosening EXPANSIN (CsEXPA10/20/21) and activating the CsCBF3‐mediated cold response pathway. Furthermore, the expression of CsBBX19 significantly reduced by light via a feedback loop involving CsHY5, which directly binds to the promoter of CsBBX19 to repress its transcription, while CsBBX19 conversely interacts with CsHY5 to reinforce its autoactivation, thereby fine‐tuning the catechins‐to‐theanine ratio and cold resilience in tea plants. Our findings underscore the central roles of CsBBX19 in light‐mediated cold response and tea quality formation, providing valuable targets for synchronously improving cold resilience and quality in tea plants.
nd0288e6a733a: Target genes of BrrTCP4, BrrTCP4a and BrrTCP4b. Summary Gene duplication is widely recognized as a significant catalyst for plant adaptive evolution. The retained duplicated genes usually undergo functional divergence to govern plant growth and stress resistance. Turnip (Brassica rapa var. rapa) shows a broad capacity for environmental adaptation. Here, we investigate how duplicated TCP4 genes modulate turnip growth and development. We identify three TCP4 paralogs, BrrTCP4, BrrTCP4a and BrrTCP4b in turnip, characterize their expression patterns and analyze sequence variation in their conserved domains. We further model their three‐dimensional structures and compare their protein–protein interactions and downstream regulatory networks. We show that BrrTCP4, BrrTCP4a and BrrTCP4b exhibit distinct expression profiles. A single mutation within the conserved TCP domain leads to differences in protein–protein interactions among BrrTCP4, BrrTCP4a and BrrTCP4b. Combined with DAP‐Seq, ChIP‐qPCR and luciferase assays, our results demonstrate that BrrTCP4 and BrrTCP4a activate BrrCOs and BrrFTs to regulate turnip flowering, while BrrTCP4b preferentially participates in the trehalose synthesis pathway by targeting TPP and TPS genes. Our research findings indicate the functional divergence of BrrTCP4, BrrTCP4a and BrrTCP4b to balance growth and stress responses in turnip, thereby advancing our understanding of how gene duplication drives functional specialization and contributes to plant evolutionary adaptation. 概括 重复基因是植物适应性进化的重要催化剂。保留下来的重复基因会发生功能分化，进而调控植物的生长发育和抗逆性。蔓菁(Brassica rapa var. rapa)隶属于十字花科芸薹属，该属经历了一次特有的全基因组三倍化事件，是研究重复基因的理想材料。因此，本文我们研究了蔓菁TCP4重复基因如何调控蔓菁的生长发育。 共线性分析发现蔓菁BrrTCP4、BrrTCP4a和BrrTCP4b是基因组复制产生的三个重复基因。我们分析了它们的表达模式和其保守结构域中的序列变异。并进一步模拟了它们的三维结构，比较了它们的互作蛋白及下游调控网络的差异。 研究结果显示BrrTCP4、BrrTCP4a和BrrTCP4b具有不同的表达模式。保守TCP结构域内的单个氨基酸突变导致了BrrTCP4和BrrTCP4a与BrrTCP4b互作蛋白的差异。结合DAP‐Seq、ChIP‐qPCR和荧光素酶实验发现，BrrTCP4和BrrTCP4a直接激活BrrCOs和BrrFTs以调控蔓菁开花，而BrrTCP4b则通过靶向TPP和TPS基因优先参与海藻糖合成途径。 我们的研究结果揭示了BrrTCP4、BrrTCP4a和BrrTCP4b重复基因发生了功能分化，这种分化平衡了蔓菁的生长发育与胁迫响应。相关研究结果加深了我们对基因重复如何驱动功能分化并促进植物适应性进化的理解。
n60fec3e0ab99: Temporal variation in carbon dioxide concentration within the crop canopy and in the atmosphere. Summary Atmospheric CO2 is rising at unprecedented rates. While its physiological effects on plants are well‐documented, the direct evolutionary impact on plant pathogens remains unknown. We investigated how CO2 interacts with other abiotic factors to shape the evolutionary potential of pathogens. We combined controlled CO2 gradient experiments with quantitative genetics to assess the interactive effects of CO2, temperature and geography on Phytophthora infestans. We measured intrinsic growth rate and aggressiveness, the two key pathogen traits, across seven geographically distinct populations and partitioned their phenotypic variance into heritability and plasticity components. Both intrinsic growth rate and aggressiveness showed a shared quadratic response to CO2, peaking c. 2000 ppm before declining. Elevated CO2 reduced phenotypic variance in aggressiveness under extreme concentrations. CO2 also reconfigured the life‐history correlation between growth and aggressiveness, shifting it from positive under ambient CO2 to negative near the optimum. Heritability exceeded plasticity for aggressiveness in most populations, indicating that virulence responds primarily through selection. Trait responses were modulated by local climate and geography, with the strongest CO2‐driven increases occurring under thermal and geographic extremes. Our results demonstrate that rising CO2 acts as a direct agent of selection, nonlinearly reshaping pathogen phenotypic architecture and life‐history strategies in a geographically heterogeneous manner.
nda5e5db10654: Workflow of gas chromatography coupled to mass spectrometry (GC‐MS)‐based 13C‐labelling analysis of plant metabolites. Summary Carbon fluxes throughout metabolic networks can be investigated experimentally through 13C‐isotope labelling experiments (13C‐ILE) and 13C‐metabolic flux analysis (13C‐MFA). 13C‐ILE involves the application of isotopically labelled substrates to a biological system to detect label distribution throughout the metabolic network, while 13C‐MFA is a computational approach that quantitatively estimates fluxes by fitting isotope‐labelling data to metabolic network models. 13C‐MFA can encompass more metabolic reactions and provide subcellular flux estimates that remain difficult to validate directly using current 13C‐ILE approaches. Overcoming major bottlenecks of 13C‐ILE is thus needed to improve and validate 13C‐MFA. Mass spectrometry (MS)‐based 13C‐ILE has been carried out mostly at isotopologue rather than isotopomer level. Isotopologues differ in their isotopic composition, while isotopomers have the same isotopic composition but at different positions within the molecule. Thus, 13C‐isotopomer approaches discriminate which atoms of a metabolite have received 13C, enabling better comprehension of the regulation of metabolic pathways. Here, we highlight the major challenges to improve MS‐based positional 13C analysis and discuss the advantages of this approach over MS‐based methods with low or no carbon‐positional resolution. We further demonstrate how positional 13C analysis has been used to estimate enzyme activity in vivo and to study plant metabolism.
n86822978e280: Box plots showing nitrogen (N) and phosphorus (P) concentrations in senesced leaves across contrasting parent materials for four site groups. Summary In theory, nutrient resorption from leaves should be higher in sites with lower soil nutrients, increasing the retention and reuse of nutrients that are limited in supply. However, evidence for this relationship has remained inconsistent for decades, particularly where the percent of nutrient resorbed is concerned. Furthermore, plant resorption responses to soil phosphorus (P) concentration remain poorly understood. Leaf nitrogen (N) and P concentrations and resorption percentages (efficiencies) were measured for 68 Australian plant species sampled across four nutrient-rich vs nutrient-poor site-pairs representing contrasting soil parent materials. N and P concentrations in senesced leaves were significantly lower on nutrient-poor than on nutrient-richer sites, enabling greater internal conservation of these nutrients on nutrient-poor sites. Resorption efficiencies averaged 45% for N and 69% for P and did not differ between contrasting soils. Though not sensitive to site, P resorption efficiency (PRE) was positively related to the proportion of labile P in leaves (R 2 = 0.54). We demonstrated for the first time that senesced leaf P concentrations and the corresponding PRE are distinctly shaped by plant adaptation to soil nutrient scarcity, and internal labile P pools, respectively. The high PRE of Australian species informs an upper bound for this process in global vegetation models.
naaf005144a0e: Schematic model illustrating MYB156‐mediated regulatory network controlling root‐sucker formation. Summary Root suckers enable clonal propagation of rooting‐recalcitrant poplars, conferring rejuvenated traits such as enhanced survival and accelerated growth. Despite widespread clonal propagation and ecological restoration, the essential genes controlling sucker development remain unidentified. MYB156 is a positive regulator of root sucker formation in white poplar (Populus davidiana × P. bolleana). MYB156 is predominantly expressed in proliferation‐competent root cells, including vascular cambium and phellogen. Gain‐ and loss‐of‐function analyses demonstrated that MYB156 overexpression enhanced root suckering and secondary growth, whereas myb156 mutants were severely compromised in both. Meanwhile, cytokinin levels increased two‐ to fivefold in roots with MYB156 overexpression but were significantly reduced in myb156 mutant roots. MYB156 directly represses IDD14 and CKX1, reducing cytokinin catabolism and alleviating IDD14‐mediated suppression of cytokinin accumulation; IDD14 RNAi lines similarly showed elevated cytokinin and enhanced suckering. Cytokinin response elements in the MYB156 promoter and MYB156 autoactivation establish a cytokinin‐MYB156 positive feedback loop amplifying cytokinin signaling in meristematic zones. Live imaging with the cytokinin response reporter TCSn:RFP demonstrated that suckering in MYB156‐overexpressing plants shifted from the phellogen to the vascular cambium. These findings establish a MYB156‐CKX1/IDD14‐cytokinin module that creates a permissive context for suckering, providing a transcriptional blueprint for clonal propagation.
nef3c043c1b3c: The meta-ecosystem framework explains spatial flows of organisms, materials, and energy across ecosystem boundaries. Parasites play crucial roles in these processes, yet they remain absent from meta-ecosystem models. Using examples from terrestrial and aquatic environments, we illustrate how parasitic organisms act as central connectors or disruptors of the flow of organisms, nutrients, and energy across ecosystem boundaries via four key mechanisms: parasite-induced host movement, behavioural changes that increase cross-ecosystem predation, host mortality, and parasite avoidance behaviour. These examples highlight the central role of parasites in driving and regulating nutrient and energy flow from catchment-to-coast, and we outline a pathway for improved integration of these parasite-mediated processes into the meta-ecosystem framework.
n720ed8e25f54: Understanding and projecting forest carbon responses to climate change remains challenging. The widely used space‐for‐time substitution (SFTS) approach assumes that ecological responses along spatial climate gradients can substitute for temporal relationships, yet agreement among spatial, temporal, and mechanistic approaches remains largely unknown. Using global satellite‐derived aboveground biomass (AGB) data, we quantified forest AGB sensitivities to spatial versus temporal climate variability, projected climate‐driven AGB changes under future emission scenarios, and compared results with Earth system models (ESMs). Spatial climate gradients explain substantially more AGB variation than temporal anomalies, with strong divergence across regions and forest ages. ESMs better reproduce spatial sensitivities than temporal ones. Temporal extrapolation generally projects future AGB gains, whereas spatial extrapolation often indicates AGB declines. These contrasts demonstrate that spatial, temporal, and model‐based approaches capture distinct facets of forest–climate coupling, and integrating them can better constrain uncertainty in carbon–climate feedbacks and improve future ecosystem projections.
n471764b5bef4: Wetlands support disproportionately high biodiversity, including waterbirds, which underpin key ecological functions and regulatory services. This has led to efforts to protect these crucial sites, but whether these protections can maintain waterbird assemblages in the face of new threats such as climate change is poorly understood. Here, we calculated functional redundancy and three metrics of functional diversity from over 45,000 waterbird censuses, spanning four decades of rising winter temperatures for 2792 protected and unprotected sites in Europe. We modelled the effect of average winter temperature and the trend over time for each of these metrics. Our results suggest functional diversity generally increased in warmer winters and over time, but redundancy declined, and the effect of temperature varied spatially and between levels of protection. This suggests abundance and distribution shifts due to climate change are altering functional diversity and resilience of waterbird assemblages both inside and outside protected areas across Europe.
ne6396ae7743f: Sacred fir (Abies religiosa) is the only roosting tree for monarch butterfly populations overwintering in Mexico, but its geographic range is expected to shrink due to climate change. A common garden experiment carried out 2019–2022 showed high seedling survival at 3400 and 3000 m, but only 6% survival at 2600 m (representing possible warmer and drier future conditions). We tested whether these survivors were genetically different from the starting population (represented by the seedlings from high‐survival gardens) using PCAdapt. We also conducted a Genotype‐Environment Association (GEA) test using climate information from source populations to identify SNP variants associated with climate gradients. PCAdapt identified 2202 outlier SNPs whose allele frequencies may have been impacted by selection. LFMM2 identified 33 SNPs associated with 5 source population climate gradients, especially winter precipitation. Minor allele frequencies (MAF) in both categories showed more fluctuation in survivors. This suggests that local climate conditions may select for genetic differences in Abies religiosa on short as well as long timescales, but fully understanding these responses requires more complete genome or transcriptome data, as well as validation by further field tests.
n5ee0655ecb78: Drone‐based measurements of free‐ranging aquatic wildlife are inevitably affected by posture variations, yet this issue has remained largely unaddressed. A widely used approach is to visually inspect body curvature based on overhead shots and exclude animals exhibiting strong body curvature, which may result in a substantially reduced dataset and inconsistent quality control. We developed a drone‐based method of estimating body measurements of dugongs using dual drones (positioned vertically and obliquely relative to the animal) whilst considering body posture (Methoddual). We reconstructed 3D coordinates of the body's dorsal line and scaled these based on altitude obtained with Real‐Time Kinematic measurements. Estimation error was evaluated using 25 free‐swimming dugongs for which direct body measures were obtained out‐of‐water and compared with a conventional method based only on overhead shots (Methodsingle). General surfacing posture of animals was further examined using 188 wild dugongs. Methoddual achieved significantly smaller absolute errors in body length (BL) than Methodsingle both when the body was relatively curved (0.039 ± 0.033 m or 2.0% ± 1.6% of BL versus 0.114 ± 0.084 m or 4.8% ± 3.8%) and straight (0.033 ± 0.028 m or 1.3% ± 1.1% versus 0.05 ± 0.042 m or 1.5% ± 1.2%). Methoddual provided reliable estimation even when the body curve ratio (ratio of apparent BL from the overhead shot to the posture‐corrected 3D BL) was lower than 0.919 (i.e., body curve is stronger), whereas Methodsingle did not. The mean body curve ratio of free‐swimming animals was 0.926 ± 0.049 (0.751–0.992; n = 188) and 31.9% had a body curve ratio below 0.919. The proposed method enables data collection from surfacing events that would otherwise have been discarded as poor quality, which may be particularly useful when encounter rate is low. This method also helps establish quantitative thresholds for data inclusion.
n77eb9875156f: Bird song plays a crucial role in sexual selection and often exhibits geographical variation, with neighboring birds typically singing more similar songs. Song sharing, created by birds learning songs or song elements from their neighbors or matching each other's song, is a key focus of research in this aspect. In this meta‐analysis, we quantified the overall effect of geographic distance on song sharing and investigated the influence of migratory tendency, repertoire size, dichromatism (as a proxy for sexual selection intensity), and habitat (urban, rural, and natural) on the focal relationship. We confirmed that song sharing decreases with geographic distance but found no overall effect of migration or repertoire size. Interestingly, this association was stronger negatively in monochromatic species and suburban habitats, potentially indicating that dichromatic species prioritize individuality in their vocal displays, while suburban birds may benefit from increased song sharing to enhance signal transmission or reduce competition. Our findings emphasize the importance of considering multiple factors when studying geographical variation in bird song. Future research should investigate other measures of song similarity and the roles of social structure and learning mechanisms.
n121d43c6568a: Urbanization promotes biological invasions, yet the relative importance of spatial versus temporal dynamics in subtropical urban ecosystems remains unclear. We investigated invasive plant communities across six habitat types in Hengqin, South China, to evaluate factors influencing their distribution across habitats and seasons. Using nonmetric multidimensional scaling (NMDS) and zero–one inflated Beta (ZOIB) models, we found that habitat type and disturbance intensity were strongly associated with invasive species distribution, explaining 58.9% of the community composition (R 2 = 0.589). Seasonal variation showed limited influence on community composition (R 2 = 0.012, p = 1.000), but the ZOIB model revealed a significant habitat × season interaction (χ152$$ {\chi}_{15}^2 $$ = 30.32, p = 0.011), indicating that seasonal effects were habitat-dependent. Invasive species exhibited significantly broader occupancy breadth than native species (Shannon index: 3.00 vs. 2.45, p = 0.024), consistent with the generalist hypothesis. Greater spatial co-occurrence among dominant invasive species (median = 0.203) compared to native species suggests that these plants share similar habitat preferences and disturbance tolerance, enabling co-occurrence in high-stress environments. The weak overall seasonal signal contrasts with phenology-based models typical of temperate zones, although seasonal effects were evident in certain habitat types (e.g., forest edge, park, and wetland declined from spring to summer). This relative stability may reflect subtropical climate and the ability of dominant invasive species to maintain year-round growth. These findings suggest that management should prioritize high-risk habitats such as roadside and wasteland, while also considering seasonal timing in habitats with marked fluctuations.
n4309aa256cb8: Understanding the spatial patterns of biodiversity and their environmental determinants is fundamental to ecology and conservation, particularly in mountainous transitional zones where species assemblages can shift rapidly. Amphibians, as highly sensitive organisms, are excellent indicators of environmental change, yet quantitative assessments of their diversity in the Huangshan Mountains—a biodiversity hotspot at the junction of the Palaearctic and Oriental realms in southern Anhui, China—remain limited. We conducted systematic line‐transect surveys across 200 grids (5 × 5 km) during the spring and autumn of 2023 and 2024, recording a total of 10,342 individuals belonging to 23 species, 20 genera, 9 families, and 2 orders. Three species (Fejervarya multistriata, Microhyla fissipes, and Bufo gargarizans) were identified as dominant, and two nationally protected species (Hoplobatrachus chinensis and Andrias davidianus) were detected. Inter‐annual alpha diversity was largely stable, with no significant differences in most metrics except species richness, but pronounced seasonal variation was observed, with spring supporting higher Shannon‐Wiener and Pielou evenness than autumn in both years. Using generalized additive models and model averaging, we found that annual precipitation and the normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI) were consistently the strongest positive predictors of Shannon‐Wiener diversity, Simpson diversity, and species richness, while species richness also declined significantly with increasing human footprint. Total beta diversity (Sørensen dissimilarity) was very high (0.981) and overwhelmingly driven by species turnover (97.86%) rather than nestedness. Partial Mantel tests and distance‐based redundancy analysis further revealed that environmental distances—particularly annual precipitation—significantly shaped overall beta diversity and its turnover component after accounting for geographic distance. These results highlight the predominant role of climatic and vegetation gradients in structuring amphibian assemblages in this subtropical mountainous region, providing baseline data to inform local conservation strategies.
n681dfc531afa: Assessment of the physical properties of concealed food items provides insight into the perceptual and cognitive mechanisms of animals. This study investigated the walnut selection behavior of wild carrion crows (Corvus corone) through two field experiments. In Experiment 1 (visual size preference), we presented walnuts with distinct visual sizes. Crows significantly preferred the larger walnut in both their first contact and final retrieval. In Experiment 2 (internal content preference), we presented walnuts of similar size but with different internal contents: filled or empty. While there was no preference for the first contact, crows significantly selected the filled walnut for final retrieval. The final selection was significantly influenced by the crows' handling behavior. In Experiment 2, the probability of switching was significantly higher when the first contact walnut was empty. Pre‐retrieval lifting behavior also played a distinct role in each experiment. In Experiment 1, lifting either the larger or smaller walnut increased the probability of it being ultimately retrieved, regardless of its size. In contrast, in Experiment 2, the number of pre‐retrieval lifts of the filled walnut significantly predicted its correct selection, whereas lifting the empty walnut had no such reinforcing effect on its retrieval. In both experiments, the probability of selecting the higher‐quality option increased with the log‐transformed weight ratio between the two walnuts, consistent with psychophysical principles of proportional weight discrimination. These findings demonstrate that wild crows flexibly integrate visual and weight information, utilizing active haptic sampling to compensate for unreliable visual cues and optimize foraging choices in a natural setting.

n1df966a66347: Large dam removals are increasingly important river restoration actions, but long-term ecological responses remain poorly understood, especially for removals involving large sediment releases. We evaluated benthic macroinvertebrate (BMI) responses following removal of the Elwha and Glines Canyon dams on the Elwha River, Washington, USA. At the time of removal (2011–2014), these were the largest dams to be dismantled worldwide. Dam removal reconnected over 90% of the watershed to anadromous fish, released more than 20 megatonnes of reservoir sediment downstream, and restored natural sediment and wood transport processes. Using nine years of monitoring data spanning periods before, during, and after dam removal, we quantified changes in BMI density, taxa richness, and community composition across five river sections exposed to different combinations of sediment disturbance, reservoir succession, and fish reintroduction. Sediment release substantially altered downstream physical habitat and was accompanied by pronounced declines in BMI density and richness, particularly downstream of both dams. Density declined by up to 95% during active dam removal but rebounded to near baseline levels within three years after peak sediment transport subsided. In contrast, taxa richness and community composition remained significantly altered three years after dam removal, with persistent reductions particularly evident among Trichoptera and long-lived taxa. Fine sediment was the environmental variable most strongly associated with changes in BMI community structure. Our results demonstrate that large dam removal can cause severe but largely transient reductions in BMI abundance while producing longer-lasting changes in taxonomic diversity and community composition. These findings highlight the importance of distinguishing between numerical and ecological recovery and suggest that recovery trajectories following large dam removal extend well beyond the period of active sediment release.
naf8ab8f7cc7b: Seasonal lake wetlands perform multiple ecological functions, including flood regulation, maintenance of land-water ecotonal habitats, and support for migratory waterbirds, and therefore play a critical role in regional biodiversity conservation. However, integrated assessments linking long-term wetland landscape reconfiguration, changes in habitat quality, and waterbird community responses remain scarce. Focusing on the Dongting Lake wetland, this study integrated land-use data, landscape metrics, habitat quality (HQ) and habitat degradation (DEG) estimated with InVEST, and waterbird species richness and community composition. Habitat-waterbird response models were developed using negative binomial generalized linear models and partial permutational multivariate analysis of variance. The results showed that the total wetland area increased from 5,019.03 km2 in 2000 to 5,118.04 km2 in 2020, whereas area of lake decreased by 533.87 km2 and reservoir/pond and marsh increased by 317.70 and 227.41 km2, respectively. For lake, percentage of landscape (PLAND) and largest patch index (LPI) both declined, indicating that wetland change was primarily characterized by internal class replacement and reconfiguration of dominant patches. Over the same period, mean HQ decreased from 0.47827 to 0.45371, whereas mean DEG increased from 0.17985 to 0.19445. Waterbird species richness showed generally weak associations with HQ, DEG, and landscape variables, although wetland LPI exhibited a positive but not significant trend during ER (IRR = 1.3763, FDR q = 0.0632). In contrast, community composition during ER was significantly associated with wetland LPI (semi-partial R2 = 0.1027, permutation p = 0.0078, FDR q = 0.0468). By jointly evaluating wetland landscape configuration, InVEST-based habitat quality, and waterbird response models, this study identified differences in habitat–waterbird associations between two recession periods. These findings provide an evidence base for adaptive management, ecological restoration of river-connected lake wetlands, and conservation of wintering waterbird habitats.
n61a537c2ab69: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Increasingly frequent seasonal droughts under rapid climate change threaten the growth stability of subtropical mixed forests across the mid‐subtropical monsoon region. In this study, we combined stable hydrogen and oxygen isotope analyses with high‐precision radial growth monitoring to explore how water source use influences the radial growth of four subtropical tree species. Three contrasting functional strategies were identified based on rooting depth and water uptake plasticity. The shallow water‐dependent species (Cupressus funebris Endl.) featured a root system concentrated in the upper soil layer and obtained 38.3% of its water from shallow layers. During the drought period, declining surface soil water availability was accompanied by low stomatal conductance and photosynthetic rates, and the species experienced net stem shrinkage of 1.1 mm. The deep‐rooted species (Michelia maudiae Dunn and Abies fabri Craib) exhibited a dual rooting strategy: Deep taproots accessed stable water in the 80–100 cm soil layer, which contributed 67.2%–75.8% of water uptake during drought, while shallow fine roots captured sporadic rainfall in the upper soil layers. During the drought period, these species maintained relatively high water potentials and positive cumulative radial growth, with annual radial growth 1.9–2.5 times that of C. funebris. The balanced‐strategy species (Liquidambar formosana Hance) displayed a relatively uniform root distribution throughout the soil profile, enabling flexible water acquisition across soil layers and sustaining the highest cumulative radial growth during the drought period. n6dadf565863a: The elemental composition of organisms and ecosystems, termed the “elementome,” fundamentally determines biological function and ecosystem processes. These elemental profiles, historically relatively stable over geological timescales, have been profoundly altered by human activity, especially since the Industrial Revolution, giving rise to a novel “human elementome.” The number and amounts of elements used biologically and nonbiologically by humans, We synthesized multidisciplinary evidence demonstrating this critical shift, characterized by pervasive imbalances in the ratios of carbon, nitrogen, and phosphorus driven by extensive anthropogenic inputs, together with the unprecedented mobilization of a wide spectrum of elements, from critical raw materials and fossil fuels to novel technological elements such as rare‐earth metals. This shift in the human elementome is therefore at the root of many of the environmental changes observed today, as it profoundly alters the cycling, distribution, and availability of chemical elements across ecosystems. These elemental perturbations have not acted in isolation but have interacted synergistically with physiological stresses induced by elevated concentrations of CO2, warming, and drought, generating complex emergent effects on life. Our findings highlight a rapid transformation of the fundamental elemental makeup of the biosphere driven by humans, with cascading ecological consequences for ecosystem function and species composition globally. This elemental perspective offers a robust framework for understanding and predicting ecosystem responses in the Anthropocene, informing strategies for conserving biodiversity and managing ecosystems.
ndd615a138213: This novel study examines how environmental and human‐related gradients influence habitat use and the community structure of medium and large terrestrial mammals in Central Amazonian white‐sand forests (campinaranas), one of the naturally rarest and least studied ecosystems in the Amazon region. n86f7d74caa67: We highlight a new paper that asks whether hunters can replace the roles of large carnivores, and argue that more insight is needed into the planet's ‘super predator’—humans. Abstract Research Highlight: Geng, Y., Mammides, C., He, R.‐C., Wang, L., Luo, K., Zhang, Z.‐Y., Wang, B., & Quan, R.‐C. (2026). Human hunters are no substitute for vanishing apex predators. Journal of Animal Ecology, 1–13. https://doi.org/10.1111/1365‐2656.70306. As large carnivores decline and humans rise to become the planet's most influential predator, scant consideration has been given to the functional roles of hunters (and fishers) in ecological communities. Apex predator‐dominated sites hosted ~30% more species and nearly 50% greater abundances of mammals. Network measures of prey populations were most robust at apex predator sites and weakest at hunter‐dominated sites. Finally, prey showed up to 2.6 times longer avoidance times following hunter presence. These striking patterns suggest that hunters do not replicate the ecological influence of the area's vanishing predators. Work like this can benefit from much more data about human predators. Specifically, ecologists can confront in careful ways the conceptual, methodological and ethical constraints of studying our own species as predators. Outcomes could include greater knowledge about the ecological influence of the planet's ‘super predator’, the underlying mechanisms, and related insight to apply to mitigation.
n0ea6bc4e04e8: Our paper investigates the crucial role of African forest elephants (Loxodonta cyclotis) on the functioning of rainforest ecosystems, through the lens of bird communities.
