Abstract African forest elephants (Loxodonta cyclotis) are critically endangered ecosystem engineers of African tropical forests. Despite their rapidly declining population trend, little is known of how forest elephants interact with other vertebrate assemblages. The area's topography allowed us to survey birds in elephant‐grazed primary forest and in adjacent portions that elephants avoid, isolating the effect of megafaunal grazing within an otherwise intact system. We additionally surveyed nearby secondary forests fragmented by human activity, contrasting the disappearance of a single ecosystem engineer against the reshaping of forest by anthropogenic disturbance. We assessed the taxonomic diversity (species richness, Shannon index), functional diversity (Rao's quadratic entropy), functional redundancy (species overlap in functional space), and composition of functional traits (abundance‐weighted trait averages). Functional diversity nevertheless increased in both the grazed and secondary forest, but at the cost of functional redundancy: in both of these habitats, the avian assemblages were taxonomically impoverished, yet functionally more dispersed, with some foraging niches negatively affected. The elephant‐grazed forest was dominated by understory and terrestrial invertivores, whereas the ungrazed forest supported frugivores and larger birds. The secondary forest, in turn, harboured a functionally distinct assemblage of open‐habitat species with high dispersal ability and divergent foraging strategies. Conversely, the adverse effects of elephant grazing on frugivores and large birds could be minimized by establishing larger reserves of lightly grazed forest, possibly alongside ungrazed refuges. Overall, our results show that loss of keystone megaherbivores has widespread consequences for other rainforest vertebrates, potentially resulting in a cascading restructuring of key ecosystem functions.
n848dc1e18583: The article provides the first conceptual framework and testable hypotheses of land tenure system in territorial carnivores across various landscape scenarios. Abstract Land tenure is a fundamental ecological process in territorial animals; it reflects how individuals establish and maintain access to space and resources. First conceptualised by Hornocker in 1969, it provides an early understanding of population dynamics. However, this critical aspect for interpreting the stability, predictability and exclusivity of a population is rarely evaluated. As land tenure provides critical insights into the spatial stability of populations and informs conservation planning, its limited integration into ecological studies remains concerning despite advances in population ecology and monitoring technologies. We attempted to build a foundation for future research that aims to measure population stability and species persistence. सारांश इलाके पर कब्ज़ा (लैंड टेन्योर) उन जानवरों के लिए एक बुनियादी पारिस्थितिक प्रक्रिया है जो अपने इलाके की रक्षा करते हैं; यह बताता है कि कैसे कोई जानवर जगह और संसाधनों तक अपनी पहुँच बनाता है और उसे बनाए रखता है। हॉर्नॉकर ने 1969 में सबसे पहले इस अवधारणा को पेश किया था, जिससे जनसंख्या गतिकी की गतिविधियों (पॉपुलेशन डायनामिक्स) को शुरुआती तौर पर समझने में मदद मिलती है। हालाँकि, किसी आबादी की स्थिरता, पूर्वानुमान और विशिष्टता को समझने के लिए इस अहम पहलू का शायद ही कभी मूल्यांकन किया जाता है। अब तक, ‘लैंड टेन्योर सिस्टम’ की कोई स्पष्ट पारिस्थितिक परिभाषा नहीं दी गई है। इस कॉन्सेप्ट को समझने के लिए, हम अपने इलाके पर कब्ज़ा रखने वाले मांसाहारी जानवरों पर पिछले 50 से ज़्यादा सालों की इकोलॉजिकल स्टडीज़ का रिव्यू करते हैं और यह समझते हैं कि अलग‐अलग तरह के जानवरों के लिए लैंड टेन्योर को कैसे मापा गया है। हम यह देखते हैं कि यह पहलू जनसंख्या गतिकी और डेमोग्राफिक प्रक्रियाओं को कैसे जोड़ता है, जिससे अलग‐अलग तरह के लैंडस्केप में प्रजातियों के संरक्षण में मदद मिलती है। इसका मकसद एक ऐसा तरीका विकसित करना है जो अलग‐अलग प्रजातियों और इलाकों में लैंड टेन्योर का मूल्यांकन करने के लिए एक ढांचा और जांचने योग्य परिकल्पनाएं प्रदान करे। चूंकि लैंड टेन्योर आबादी की स्थानिक स्थिरता के बारे में महत्वपूर्ण जानकारी देता है और संरक्षण की योजना बनाने में मदद करता है, इसलिए आबादी की पारिस्थितिकी और निगरानी तकनीकों में प्रगति के बावजूद पारिस्थितिक अध्ययनों में इसका सीमित एकीकरण चिंता का विषय बना हुआ है। हमने भविष्य के शोध के लिए एक आधार बनाने की कोशिश की है जिसका मकसद आबादी की स्थिरता और प्रजातियों के बने रहने को मापना है।
nb18daad1f74c: Our findings indicate that elevated plant colonisation drives shifts towards faster‐growing, decomposition‐oriented microbial communities. Abstract Colonisation by previously absent plants is increasing under global environmental change. Colonist establishment can alter plant community composition and could subsequently affect soil microbial communities. Plant and microbial communities were surveyed 9 years after initial seed addition. Colonist cover was higher in the early succession site. Across both sites, evidence indicated that higher colonist cover led to communities with faster growth strategies, altered belowground resource acquisition strategies, and—at the early succession site—lowered taxonomic diversity. Through these changes in plant community composition, higher colonist cover was associated with less diverse prokaryote communities characterised by elevated metabolic activity and cellular replication, and a higher abundance of fungal saprotrophs. Colonist cover was only weakly linked to other microbial functional groups at the early succession site, with no observed links to obligate fungi, despite colonist abundance being highest there. At the late succession site, higher cover of fast‐growing colonists was associated with prokaryote communities exhibiting lower metabolic activity and greater obligate fungal abundance. Also at the late succession site, plots with more colonist seed additions supported higher prokaryote diversity and greater abundance of fungal obligates than unsown plots, regardless of current plant composition. Synthesis: Our findings indicate that elevated plant colonisation drives shifts towards faster‐growing, decomposition‐oriented microbial communities. However, associations between plant colonists and microbial communities were stronger at the late succession site, even though colonist cover was higher in the early succession site. Practitioners should therefore consider belowground impacts of plant colonisation across all grasslands, and not only where effects on plant community composition are most visible.
n2aef9f241866: Exotic dominance can leave behind soil microbial legacies that favour exotic plants over natives. Abstract Ecosystems worldwide are undergoing a pervasive transition toward exotic‐dominated states, a shift that threatens biodiversity and disrupts key ecosystem functions. Although positive abiotic feedbacks are frequently cited as drivers of these transitions, the microbial mechanisms involved remain poorly understood. In a two‐phase greenhouse experiment, we conditioned soils along a gradient of increasing exotic plant dominance using 10 exotic and 10 native species. We then assessed plant performance on these soil microbial inocula under no, intraspecific and interspecific competition. We found that increasing exotic dominance progressively reshaped soil microbial communities in ways that favoured exotic over native growth, without altering competitive strengths. This growth asymmetry was tightly linked to arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF), whose richness increased with exotic dominance and was positively correlated with exotic performance. Complementary field surveys of the same exotic species confirmed a positive correlation between their abundance and AMF richness in natural communities. Synthesis. Our findings demonstrate that increasing dominance of exotic plants can generate microbial legacies that progressively favour exotic plants over native plants. These microbial legacies provide a mechanism linking changes in plant community structure to subsequent competitive interactions and offer a framework for understanding how biotic interactions, particularly those involving soil mutualists, can contribute to the persistence and spread of invasive plants. 中文摘要 全球生态系统正在普遍向外来植物占优势的状态转变，这一转变威胁生物多样性并扰乱关键生态系统功能。尽管正向非生物反馈常被认为是这类生态转变的驱动因素，但其中涉及的微生物机制仍知之甚少。 本研究开展两阶段温室实验，选取10种外来植物和10种本地植物，沿外来植物优势度递增梯度完成土壤驯化处理。随后在无竞争、种内竞争和种间竞争条件下，评估植物在上述土壤微生物接种环境中的生长表现。 研究发现，外来植物优势度的增加会逐步重塑土壤微生物群落结构，形成利于外来植物生长、而非本地植物生长的格局，且不会改变物种竞争强度。这种生长不对称性与丛枝菌根真菌密切相关:丛枝菌根真菌丰富度随外来植物优势度升高而增加，且与外来植物生长表现呈正相关。针对相同外来物种的野外补充调查进一步证实，自然群落中外来植物多度与丛枝菌根真菌丰富度存在显著正相关关系。 综上，外来植物优势度的增加可以形成有利于外来植物而非本土植物的土壤微生物遗留效应，而且这种作用会随外来植物优势度提高而增强。这些遗留效应揭示了植物群落结构变化影响后续竞争关系的潜在机制，并为理解生物相互作用，尤其是土壤互惠生物介导的相互作用，如何促进入侵植物的持续存在和扩散提供了理论框架。
nde9de303f3e6: Collectively, these findings provide direct experimental evidence that plants act as central hubs that reconfigure the biodiversity‐stability relationship by mediating green‐brown food web coupling, and emphasise that maintaining plant integrity is critical for sustaining high multifunctionality and biologically buffered stability under global change. Abstract Direct evidence of how plants regulate soil biodiversity–ecosystem stability relationships remains scarce, as the coupling between aboveground and belowground components makes it methodologically challenging to isolate plant‐mediated effects from the independent role of soil biota. Collectively, these findings provide direct experimental evidence that plants act as central hubs that reconfigure the biodiversity‐stability relationship by mediating green‐brown food web coupling, and emphasise that maintaining plant integrity is critical for sustaining high multifunctionality and biologically buffered stability under global change.
n462c1857a9cd: Context dependence can sometimes seem overwhelming in ecology, but—in this study—trends were largely predictable when we considered how causal drivers and limiting factors likely vary across different ecological conditions. Abstract Context dependence can impede accurate prediction in ecology, including plant colonisation. Although it is well established that ecology is complicated, most studies in ecology focus on one or two factors at a time and most experiments run for less than 3 years. Synthesis: Context dependence can sometimes seem overwhelming in ecology, but—in this study—trends were largely predictable when we considered how causal drivers and limiting factors likely vary across different ecological conditions. Our study highlights the value of long‐term multifactorial experiments and suggests that the interplay of limiting factors can help predict mechanistic context dependence in plant colonisation.
ne1127af09c50: India is a major centre of rice diversity, where long‐term cultivation across contrasting environments has generated substantial genomic and phenotypic variation. n8cb3ea9ed3ae: Contact zones, where related taxa breed sympatrically, provide natural laboratories for studying phylogeography and speciation. n12c8fc60a51c: A single amino‐acid substitution reprograms ROP6 from PIN stabilization to endocytic degradation. na9a42914bee6: Ancestral lifestyle reconstruction across the phylogeny of the 107 analysed fungal genomes. n07cb246c8b4a: Study site and focal species. Summary Canopy and leaf temperatures often diverge from air temperature, influencing photosynthesis, water loss, and heat stress.
